sections.label: Three areas Deputy Prime Minister covered
sections.summary: The speaker will address jobs and Jobs-Skills Integrators, the CPF income ceiling, and HDB resale flat grants.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In the second part, I will address three specific areas covered by the Deputy Prime Minister: one, Jobs and the new Jobs-Skills Integrators; two, the raising of the CPF income ceiling; and three, the increased grants for buyers of HDB resale flats.

sections.label: Social trends in Singapore
sections.summary: The speaker describes an ageing population, views on social mobility, and meritocracy favouring the well-off.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: For those of us on the ground, our social trends are clear – a rapidly ageing population, a belief that social mobility for younger Singaporeans contrasts markedly with that in our parents' generation and a view that meritocracy has developed a perverse edge, allowing the well-off to move ahead much faster than the broad middle-class.

sections.label: Threat of two Singapores
sections.summary: Without more action, the potential emergence of two Singapores may become reality.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: If Singapore does not do more, a threat that has loomed large on the horizon in the last few years, of the potential emergence of "two Singapores", may become reality.

sections.label: Redistributive policies and fiscal intervention
sections.summary: Past efforts allow redistributive proposals today, and the Budget raises taxes on high-end property and luxury vehicles.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: It is not lost on many Singaporeans including the Workers' Party that it is because of these efforts and those of their forebears that we have the capacity to propose other redistributive policies for our fellow Singaporeans today.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I note the moves through the Budget to better equalise opportunities through fiscal intervention, such as raising taxes and duties for high-end property and luxury vehicles.

sections.label: Jobs-Skills Integrators pilot sectors
sections.summary: Jobs-Skills Integrators are piloted for precision engineering, resale and wholesale trade, with 3,000 PMET jobs projected by 2020.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The Deputy Prime Minister announced that the Jobs-Skills Integrators are being piloted for the precision engineering, resale and wholesale trade sectors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In a 2016 press release on the Industry Transformation Map, or ITM, for the precision engineering sector with respect to digital manufacturing, the then-Minister of Trade and Industry reported that the move towards digital manufacturing would see the creation of 3,000 PMET jobs by 2020.

sections.label: First Industry Transformation roadmap funding
sections.summary: A sum of $4.5 billion was committed to the first Industry Transformation roadmap.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: A sum of $4.5 billion was committed to the first Industry Transformation roadmap.

sections.label: WSG local employment agencies results
sections.summary: WSG said it worked with four local employment agencies but placement rate was less than 50%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Crucially, this move came after WSG stated that it had worked with four local employment agencies, but with I quote "lacklustre results" where the placement rate was less than 50%.

sections.label: Senior Employment Credit extension support
sections.summary: The speaker supports extending the Senior Employment Credit to 2025, which pays up to 8% of wages up to $4,000 monthly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: For this reason, I support the extension of the Senior Employment Credit (SEC) up to 2025.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The SEC pays up to 8% of wages, up to a salary of $4,000 a month.

sections.label: Workers' Party supports income ceiling rise
sections.summary: The Workers' Party supports raising the income ceiling to $8,000 because of retirement adequacy importance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Because of the importance of retirement adequacy in the longer term, the Workers' Party supports the rise of the income ceiling to $8,000.

sections.label: Ordinary Account allocation reduction proposal
sections.summary: The speaker proposes reducing Ordinary Account allocation by 1% to 2% in favour of the Special Account alongside the salary ceiling hike.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: To achieve the Finance Minister's policy intent of better retirement adequacy, a reduction in the range of 1% to 2% in the allocation to the Ordinary Account from one's early years in favour of the higher interest-bearing Special Account in step with the salary ceiling hike would serve the retirement needs of Singaporeans better.

sections.label: Short-wait flats and CPF grants
sections.summary: The Minister for National Development alluded to more short-wait flats and higher CPF grants for resale flat buyers were announced.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: From this it would appear that at the highest levels, the Government intends to intensify its efforts in this regard.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Also, in a Facebook post of 12 February, the Minister for National Development alluded to going beyond building an additional 2,000 to 3,000 short-wait flats by 2025.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The Minister said that the HDB will recalibrate its building programme from 2025, so that short-wait time flats form a larger proportion of our new flat supply than before.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: While the details for the moment are restricted to broad thinking, these public pronouncements were followed shortly by the Deputy Prime Minister's Budget Day announcement of higher CPF grants for resale flat buyers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Would they feed into higher prices and only make a future correction even sharper when the reality of lease decay for resale fats set in?

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I hope the Minister can share the Government's thinking behind this move and the assessment of its intended effects, particularly in view of 11 quarters of growth in HDB resale prices.

sections.label: BEPS impact and budget office
sections.summary: The occasional paper could not shed light on BEPS impact, and the Workers' Party recalls its proposal for a Parliamentary Budget Office.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Like the Finance Minister's Budget, the occasional paper was unable to shed significant light on the impact of the Base Erosion and Profit Shifting 2.0 (BEPS) on our fiscal position.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: However, it did hypothesise the prospects of greater corporate tax revenue collection under Pillar Two, which it said is expected not to deliver any fiscal upsides as any additional revenue would be ploughed back to encourage investments into Singapore by way of grants.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: With the Minister’s announcement in this Budget to top up the National Productivity Fund by $4 billion for, I quote, "investment promotion", the impact of BEPS is likely to be a significant question mark with regard to the Ministry’s medium-term fiscal outlook.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Be that as it may, the Workers' Party looks forward to more of such papers and recalls its proposal two budget cycles ago for the establishment of a Parliamentary Budget Office for a closer scrutiny of the Government's budget.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In view of tighter fiscal environment in the years to come as predicted by the occasional paper, such an office would hold much promise for greater Parliamentary and public scrutiny on Government expenditure and whether programs are worth the taxpayer monies that have been allocated to them.

sections.label: Assurance Package and GST Vouchers
sections.summary: The Government upsized the Assurance Package and GST Vouchers and added Cost-of-Living Special Payments, CDC Vouchers, U-Save and CDA top-ups.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: The further upsizing of the Assurance Package and the permanent GST Vouchers, coupled with the newly introduced Cost-of-Living Special Payments, the increased Community Development Council (CDC) Vouchers, doubling of U-Save and topping up of the Child Development Account (CDA), demonstrates the Government's commitment to journey through this difficult period of rising cost with Singaporeans.

sections.label: Senior care centres and fund top-ups
sections.summary: More senior care centres are being built, and the speaker supports $500 million for the Eldercare Fund and $1.5 billion for Medifund.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: We are also building more senior care centres at the neighbourhoods to serve seniors who need more longer-term chronic care services at more convenient locations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: Hence, I support the top-ups of the Eldercare Fund by $500 million and the Medifund by $1.5 billion.

sections.label: Buyer Stamp Duty and ARF adjustments
sections.summary: Higher marginal Buyer Stamp Duty and an upward ARF adjustment steepen tax progressivity so the better-off contribute more.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: The higher marginal Buyer Stamp Duty for higher-value properties and the upward adjustment of the Additional Registration Fee (ARF) is very much in keeping with our approach to steepen the progressivity of our tax structure and where the better-off contribute more.

sections.label: Concern over raising the ceiling
sections.summary: The speaker worries that raising the ceiling now would add business costs and reduce middle-income households' take-home pay amid high inflation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: As inflation is expected to stay elevated in the next few years, my concern is that raising the ceiling at this juncture would add further cost pressures to businesses and also reduce the take home pay of middle-income households, just when they need the cash to meet the higher cost needs.

sections.label: US Inflation Reduction Act
sections.summary: Last year the US introduced the US$369 billion Inflation Reduction Act.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: Last year, the US introduced the US$369 billion Inflation Reduction Act.

sections.label: Enterprise Innovation Scheme and SME support
sections.summary: The new Enterprise Innovation Scheme enhances tax deductions with cash conversion up to $20,000, alongside the SME Co-Investment Fund and Global Enterprises initiative.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: To nurture and sustain pervasive innovations, the new Enterprise Innovation Scheme is introduced, under which tax deductions are enhanced.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: There is also a new cash conversion component of up to $20,000 for companies yet to turn profitable.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: To help support scaling up of the local enterprises, the SME Co-Investment Fund and the Global Enterprises initiative are there to invest and support promising companies to internationalise and to seek global markets.

sections.label: Terminal cost to Government
sections.summary: The terminal cost about $1.7 billion, a major financial outlay for the Government then.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: At a cost of about $1.7 billion, the terminal was a major financial outlay for the Government then.

sections.label: Fiscal management against external shocks
sections.summary: Prudent fiscal management today is the best defence against external shocks, with expenditure projected to hit 20% of GDP and operating expenditure rising faster.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: Our best defence against any future external shocks, whether it is a black swan event or any catastrophic incident is responsible and prudent fiscal management today.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: We are heading towards a spending milestone where expenditures is projected to hit 20% of our GDP.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: Our operating expenditure will keep rising and at a faster pace in the years ahead.

sections.label: Reserves uses and returns
sections.summary: Reserves buffer against crisis, and their returns are a main income source to finance the budget and maintain confidence in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: Reserves are not only to buffer against a crisis but its returns are also a main source of income to finance the budget, as well as to help maintain confidence in Singapore.

sections.label: Handouts and price escalation risk
sections.summary: Huge government handouts have created vicious price escalation in other countries, and the member asks the Deputy Prime Minister to assess this risk in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: This has, in fact, already happened in other countries where huge government handouts had created a vicious escalation in prices.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: So, I would like to ask Deputy Prime Minister for his assessment of such risk in Singapore.

sections.label: DTT, fund top-up, tax scheme
sections.summary: Deputy Prime Minister Wong announced the Domestic Top Up Tax planned for 2025, a $4 billion National Productivity Fund top-up, and a new Enterprise Innovation Scheme.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: Deputy Prime Minister Wong announced that the implementation of Singapore's Domestic Top Up Tax (DTT) is currently planned for 2025.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: He also announced the $4 billion top-up of the National Productivity Fund to include investment promotion as a supportable activity, along with a very generous new Enterprise Innovation Scheme (EIS) with up to 400% tax deductions on qualifying expenditure, with potential to enjoy tax savings of nearly 70% of investments.

sections.label: Government R&D investment
sections.summary: The Government has committed significant resources to R&D, including $25 billion from 2021 to 2025 to catalyse research, innovation and enterprise.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: On top of these, the Government has committed significant resources to R&D over the years, including investing $25 billion from 2021 to 2025 to catalyse research, innovation and enterprise.

sections.label: Special transfers and fiscal gap
sections.summary: Special transfers were revised to $9.2 billion in FY2022, and the Ministry of Finance projected a $7.5 billion to $15 billion fiscal gap from 2026 to 2030.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: Special transfers, including top-ups to endowment funds and trust funds, were revised to $9.2 billion in FY2022, representing a $2.9 billion increase from the estimated figure.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: The Occasional Paper put out by the Ministry of Finance projected a fiscal gap of $7.5 billion to $15 billion over the medium term from 2026 to 2030 mainly to fund healthcare, uplifting lower-wage workers and improving childhood education.

sections.label: Progressive taxes and fiscal discipline
sections.summary: The passage says taxes should stay progressive, citing stamp duty increases, and that schemes should be reviewed and programmes retired.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: Taking the cue from the Government's recent tax moves, it is right that we continue to make our taxes progressive, as in the case of this year's increase in stamp duties for higher-end properties and luxury cars.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: With limited fiscal space, it is imperative that the Government continuously review schemes to assess value for money and have the discipline to retire programmes appropriately.

sections.label: COVID-19 spending and excess resources
sections.summary: The Government spent $72 billion on COVID-19, drew $40 billion from reserves, and had $56 billion of excess resources over three years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: In the end, the Government spent a total of $72 billion, fighting COVID-19.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The Government did not need to draw $72 billion from the reserves but only $40 billion because it was able to find $32 billion of excess fiscal resources in the Budgets of 2020 to 2022 to fund the balance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: On top of that, in the same three years, the Government was able to set aside $24 billion from the Budget to top up various endowment and trust funds whose spending are for future years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Hence, we can say that there is a total of $56 billion – $32 billion plus $24 billion – of excess resources in the Budgets over the past three financial years.

sections.label: NIRC record in 2023
sections.summary: In 2023, the NIRC reached a new record of $23.5 billion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: In 2023, the NIRC has reached a new record of $23.5 billion.

sections.label: Affordable and Millennial housing schemes
sections.summary: The Affordable Homes Scheme and Millennial Apartments Scheme will not draw down the reserves.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The Affordable Homes Scheme and Millennial Apartments Scheme will not draw down the reserves.

sections.label: PSP alternative Budget tax proposals
sections.summary: PSP proposes reversing some Budget 2022 and 2023 tax increases, reverting GST to 7% and limiting property taxes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: In the alternative Budget, PSP proposes that some of the tax increases of Budget 2022 and 2023 should be reversed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: GST will be reverted to 7% and property taxes for owner-occupied properties will be restricted to those with annual value of more than $50,000.

sections.label: PSP EP holder levy
sections.summary: PSP's alternative Budget introduces a $1,200 monthly levy on Employment Pass holders, recommended since 2021, to level the playing field.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: In the alternative Budget, to level the playing field between Singaporeans and foreign employees, PSP will introduce a $1,200 monthly levy on EP holders, which we have recommended since 2021.

sections.label: PSP $1 billion social spending
sections.summary: PSP proposes $1 billion to double ComCare payouts and give allowances to caregivers and stay-at-home parents, using excess fiscal resources.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Next, PSP proposes budgeting $1 billion to help the disadvantaged segments of our society by doubling the ComCare payout for the poor and providing an allowance for caregivers and stay-at-home parents in recognition of their sacrifices and contribution to society.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: But PSP has pointed out that in fact, there are excess fiscal resources in the Budget that can be deployed better.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: This is before further potential savings that we can have from spending cuts partly due to the end of the COVID-19 pandemic.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: For a start, we have increased net spending by about $8 billion – a fraction of the excess resources we have – to implement long-term programmes that will: one, proactively deploy excess fiscal resources in the Budget for the benefit of the current generation of Singaporeans; two, promote the financial security of the middle-class, who are the bedrock of the society, as a priority; and three, reduce socioeconomic ills caused by high property prices by resetting our public housing policy and eventually wean off Singapore's over-dependence on property as an engine of economic growth.

sections.label: Business sentiment and challenges
sections.summary: Business satisfaction rose to 52%, trade grew 17.7% to S$1.37 trillion, but 32% of businesses were negatively impacted and cited costs and manpower.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Business sentiments in Singapore are more positive now with 52% of the businesses being satisfied with the current business climate in Singapore compared to 37% in the prior year.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Trade grew 17.7% to reach S$1.37 trillion, and, as shared by the Deputy Prime Minister on Budget Day, Singapore’s economy grew 3.6% with resident unemployment below pre-pandemic levels, at 2.8%.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: However, as we entered 2023, businesses which had expressed optimism about the reopening of the global economy are now conveying a more cautious outlook as new disruptions surface and geopolitical fault lines deepen: 32% of the businesses stated that they had been negatively impacted over the past six months, with an average decline in revenue of 25%; 66% of both large and small companies have called out: one, overall business cost as their top challenge; two, availability of manpower; and three, retention of manpower following close behind.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: They were certainly relieved to hear the Deputy Prime Minister extend the Energy Efficiency Grant (EFG) and the Enterprise Financing Scheme (EFS) to March 2024.

sections.label: Business transformation and productivity fund
sections.summary: 64% of businesses see transformation and upskilling as important, and welcome a S$4 billion top-up for the National Productivity Fund.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In short, the paradigm has shifted and 64% of our businesses recognise that it is very important to drive transformation, build capabilities and upskill their workers to become more productive and more competitive.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: They are glad that there will be a S$4 billion top-up for the National Productivity Fund (NPF) to support their efforts.

sections.label: SGX climate reporting for SMEs
sections.summary: With SGX mandatory climate reporting for listed companies from 2023, SMEs will increasingly face similar expectations as value chain partners.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: With the Singapore Exchange (SGX) implementing mandatory climate reporting for listed companies in selected sectors from 2023, SMEs will increasingly be held to similar expectations as they are critical value chain partners.

sections.label: Enhanced tax deductions for innovation
sections.summary: Enhanced tax deductions to 400% of qualifying expenditure on five categories, including polytechnic and ITE innovation, show government support for innovation.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: With the enhanced tax deductions to 400% of qualifying expenditure on five categories including innovation carried out with the polytechnics and ITE, and even an upfront cash for companies that pay little or no taxes, it is clear that the Government is encouraging innovation and prepared to co-share risks.

sections.label: SME Co-Investment Fund boost
sections.summary: Budget 2023 adds $150 million to the SME Co-Investment Fund and enhances the Singapore Global Enterprises initiative, which could help SMEs build lasting Singapore brands.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The additional $150 million for the SME Co-Investment Fund and the enhancement to the Singapore Global Enterprises initiative in Budget 2023 could be helpful to our small to medium-sized companies to build Singapore brands that can last.

sections.label: Budget 2023 GST support
sections.summary: Many are comforted that Budget 2023 gives assurance and extra lift to lower to middle income households and retirees to defray the GST rate increase.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Many are comforted that Budget 2023 gives assurance and extra lift for the lower to middle income households and retirees to defray the GST rate increase.

sections.label: Property affordability and wealthy family offices
sections.summary: A UBS report says most households cannot afford property in top financial centres without inheritance, and the question asks how MAS and MND will help Singaporeans own residential real estate amid wealthy family offices.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In a UBS Global Real Estate Bubble Index Report, it is reported that most households can no longer afford to buy property in the top financial centres of the world without a substantial inheritance.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: How does MAS and MND collectively plan to help ensure that Singaporeans can still get to own our limited residential real estate even as we welcome wealthy family offices into Singapore, whose purchasing power will inevitably drive up property sale and rental prices?

sections.label: Seniors Go Digital and vulnerable
sections.summary: Technology cannot replace human contact and must not forget the vulnerable, so those who cannot go digital must not be denied essential services.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Technology cannot replace the human contact and encounter, and must not forget the vulnerable.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: So while the Government and the army of volunteers help our Seniors Go Digital, and support their efforts to keep up with times, there will be many who just cannot go digital and these people must not be denied of essential services.

sections.label: Jobs-Skills Integrators and CET
sections.summary: Lawrence Wong introduced Jobs-Skills Integrators to match industries' skills gaps, and the question asks how CET curriculum and ITMs push industry boundaries and which key industries are targeted.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
sentences.text: To better enhance the scheme, Deputy Prime Minister Lawrence Wong introduced the Jobs-Skills Integrators to better match the industries' skills gap and the learning required to be put in place.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
sentences.text: I appreciate the concept and see the need to plug this gap, but would like to further understand how the current CET curriculum available and ITMs that have made significant progress are pushing the boundaries for industries.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
sentences.text: Also, can Deputy Prime Minister Wong outline some of the key industries in which we are trying to develop a competitive advantage in and how the Enterprise Innovation Scheme can complement ITMs and imbue a stronger innovative culture?

sections.label: Overseas Network and Expertise Pass
sections.summary: The Overseas Network and Expertise Pass was introduced to fill gaps for new emerging growth areas like digital and sustainability.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
sentences.text: Recently, the Overseas Network and Expertise Pass was introduced as we hope to fill the gaps for new emerging growth areas like the digital and sustainability space.

sections.label: Clean energy supply and government role
sections.summary: Singapore lacks natural resources and land, so the Government acts as catalyst, regulator and facilitator to bring clean energy from other geographies.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
sentences.text: For example, a critical resource like energy supply, one that our nation clearly requires from residential to commercial, or industrial demands.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
sentences.text: We have long known that Singapore has no natural resources, limited land space and no geological attributes to generate much electricity from clean energy sources.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
sentences.text: But for us to meet our climate targets, we need the value chain to be in place to transport the clean energy sources from other geographies to Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
sentences.text: The Government has utilised different options to pilot projects, build partnerships with different countries and urged the private sector to be a strong proponent in developing solutions that may be feasible for our needs.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
sentences.text: Thus far, the Government's role continues to be that of a catalyst, a regulator and a facilitator.

sections.label: Global inflation and COE prices
sections.summary: The passage states there is high global inflation with sluggish economic growth, and Certificate of Entitlement prices remain high.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: First, there is high global inflation, coupled with sluggish economic growth.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: Second, the Certificate of Entitlement (COE) prices remain high.

sections.label: Healthcare waits and GST increase
sections.summary: The passage cites waits for public healthcare appointments caused by the pandemic and global competition for healthcare manpower, and the GST increase.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: And fourth, the wait for appointments in our public healthcare system brought about by the pandemic and exacerbated by the global competition for nursing and other healthcare manpower.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: And of course, the Goods and Services Tax (GST) increase.

sections.label: Budget support measures
sections.summary: This year's Budget includes enhanced GST Vouchers, additional CDC Vouchers, an Assurance Package for cost-of-living, and help for families with young children.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: Examples of these in this year's Budget include enhanced GST Vouchers, additional CDC Vouchers, an Assurance Package that addresses rising cost-of-living and aims to support, amongst others, students and seniors, help for families with young children.

sections.label: Singapore staying relevant and nimble
sections.summary: The passage says Singapore must stay relevant, be nimble and embrace change, offering services and products other countries want, with skillsets, attitude and values.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: If there is one truism in geopolitics, it is that no one owes us a living, especially for a city state that is nothing more than a little red dot on many maps.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: We have to stay relevant, be nimble and embrace change.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: Staying relevant means we have to offer the services and products that other countries want and pay a good price for.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: In 2014, Sir, I said in this House that for Singapore to survive and prosper, we need to have the relevant skillsets, right attitude and the moral compass and values.

sections.label: GSTV Cash increases
sections.summary: GSTV Cash was raised to $400 in 2022 and $500 in 2023, and this Budget provides increases to $700 and then $850 in 2024.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: In last year's Budget, Deputy Prime Minister Wong announced that this GSTV – Cash would be raised to $400 in 2022 and $500 in 2023, for eligible Singaporeans living in smaller flats.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: But this year, the Budget has outdone itself, because before the increase to $500 in cash can be implemented this year, this Budget provides for another increase, to $700, and then, to $850 in 2024, versus just $400 in 2022.

sections.label: GST Voucher Cash and Assurance Package
sections.summary: GST Voucher Cash has been doubled permanently for one in two adult Singaporeans, with $2.4 billion top-ups to the GST Voucher Fund in two Budgets.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: In other words, within the space of two Budgets, two fiscal years, GST Voucher – Cash has been essentially doubled, permanently, for every one in two adult Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: Indeed, this year's Budget tops up the GST Voucher Fund by $2.4 billion, after a similar top up of $2.4 billion last year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: Very decisive and a real commitment to keep this going permanently.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: And separately, under the Assurance Package, a 65-year-old retiree who owns no more than one property will receive – on top of the $700 cash under the GST Voucher Scheme, this retiree will receive another $1,300, in cash, this year alone, under the Assurance Package.

sections.label: Progressive wages for lower-wage workers
sections.summary: It sets rising minimum gross monthly wages for cooks, conservancy cleaners and cashiers from 2023 to 2028.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: For a cook in a full-service F&B outlet, monthly gross wage will be at least $2,050 starting from this March, going up to at least $2,380 in March 2025.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: For a conservancy cleaner, at least $1,795 from this July, going up to $2,835 by July 2028.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: For a cashier, at least $1,850 already from last September, going up to at least $2,175 by next September.

sections.label: Progressive Wage Credit Scheme Fund top-up
sections.summary: This Budget tops up $2.4 billion to the Progressive Wage Credit Scheme Fund, after a $2.8 billion top-up last year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: In this Budget, topping up $2.4 billion to the Progressive Wage Credit Scheme Fund after a top up of $2.8 billion last year.

sections.label: Expenditure growth and GDP share
sections.summary: Total operating and developmental expenditure rose from $28 billion, 17% of GDP, two decades ago to $104 billion, kept at 16% of GDP.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: Back then, total operating and developmental expenditure was $28 billion or 17% of Gross Domestic Product (GDP).

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: Fast forward two decades, in this year's Budget, it is $104 billion – four times – but we have managed to keep this at 16% of GDP.

sections.label: NIR contribution growth
sections.summary: NII contribution was $2.4 billion, 1% of GDP, in 2002, and NIR contribution is now $24 billion, 4% of GDP.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: NII contribution in 2002 was $2.4 billion, 1% of GDP.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: Today, NIR contribution is $24 billion or 4% of GDP.

sections.label: MAS 2023 inflation projections
sections.summary: MAS expects CPI-All Items inflation of 5.5% to 6.5% and core inflation averaging 3.5% to 4.5% in 2023.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) expects inflation to stay high in 2023, with the Consumer Price Index for All Items (CPI-All Items) inflation projected to come in at between 5.5% and 6.5%, and even core inflation is expected to average 3.5% to 4.5%, both of which includes the effect of the 1% increase in GST rates this year and likely next year as well.

sections.label: FY2021 and FY2022 fiscal position
sections.summary: FY2021 revenues were about $5.9 billion higher and the primary deficit $13.4 billion smaller than estimated, turning an expected $11 billion deficit into a $1.9 billion surplus.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: In FY 2021, actual operating revenues were about $5.9 billion higher, while the primary deficit was $13.4 billion smaller than initially estimated in Budget 2021.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: This meant that instead of a S$11 billion overall deficit that was expected, the Government's fiscal position in FY2021 turned out to be a surplus of $1.9 billion instead!

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Similarly, in FY 2022, operating revenues are now expected to be $8.5 billion higher than what was initially estimated in Budget 2022.

sections.label: BEPS 2.0 international tax reform
sections.summary: BEPS 2.0 is described as one of the most significant reforms to international tax rules to ensure multinational enterprises pay a fair share of tax wherever they operate.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: BEPS 2.0 is one of the most significant reforms to international tax rules to ensure that Multinational Enterprises (MNEs) pay a fair share of tax wherever they operate.

sections.label: Possible start in early 2024
sections.summary: If all goes according to plan, this could happen in less than a year's time, in the beginning of 2024.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: If all goes according to plan, this could happen in less than a year’s time, in the beginning of 2024.

sections.label: Luxury property sales despite ABSD
sections.summary: Despite hefty ABSD rates for foreigners, luxury purchases included EDEN sold to a single family for $293 million and 20 Canninghill Piers units for $87.6 million.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Despite hefty ABSD rates for foreigners, that did not stop an entire luxury condo project, EDEN, from being sold to a single family for $293 million, for a single buyer to purchase 20 units in Canninghill Piers for $87.6 million or for a single penthouse unit at Les Maison Nassim to be sold for $75 million last year.

sections.label: Higher ARF and PARF effects
sections.summary: The move would make a Ferrari Roma cost about 23% more from the higher ARF, with capped PARF rebates losing about 22% of the selling price.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: With the move, not only would a Ferrari Roma cost about 23% more as a result of the higher ARF, the capped PARF rebates would mean about 22% of the selling price would be lost as well, resulting in a more meaningful contribution of high-end vehicle-related taxes to Government revenues.

sections.label: WMCR change effects on mothers
sections.summary: Mothers earning under $2,610 are not better off, those above $3,810 are worse off, and only those earning $2,610 to $3,810 save $0 to $40 yearly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Essentially, for mothers who earn less than $2,610 a month, they would not be better off as they would not have paid taxes at all even under the prior methodology, while mothers earning more than $3,810 a month and above will be worse off.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The only group of mothers who would be better off are those earning between $2,610 and $3,810 a month, and the extent of their tax savings range from a grand $0 to $40 in total tax savings a year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Based on my estimates of working mothers' income within married couples in resident households, roughly 20% of mothers will benefit from the WMCR change to the tune of up to $40, while the remaining 80% of mothers will either be unaffected or worse off.

sections.label: CPF salary ceiling benefits
sections.summary: A worker could gain $1,530 in additional employers' CPF contributions in 2026 with the raised monthly salary ceiling, rising to $2,040 if the annual ceiling is raised in tandem.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: When fully implemented in 2026, he or she could benefit from $1,530 worth of additional employers’ CPF contributions with the raised monthly salary ceiling.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: However, should the annual salary ceiling be raised in tandem, this would rise to $2,040 implying that the same worker will benefit from an increased CPF contribution of $510 a year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Yet, if the annual salary ceiling was raised in tandem, his or her CPF balances will be higher by $4,420 a year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: In Budget 2015, it was said that the higher salary ceiling will cover wages up to the 80th percentile of resident incomes.

sections.label: FY2023 government deficit
sections.summary: The Government expects a modest deficit of S$0.4 billion in FY2023.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: (In Mandarin):   Looking into FY2023, I note that the Government expects a modest deficit of S$0.4 billion.

sections.label: Working mothers' WMCR change
sections.summary: Roughly 20% of mothers will benefit from the WMCR change while 80% will be unaffected or worse off.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Based on my estimates of working mothers' income within married couples, roughly 20% of mothers will benefit from the WMCR change while the remaining 80% of mothers will either be unaffected or worse off.

sections.label: Tax revenue and GDP growth
sections.summary: Singapore's tax revenue has grown with GDP, financing Government spending, but growth must fall to a more moderate level near the technology frontier.

sentences.speaker: Prof Hoon Hian Teck (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Over the years, Singapore's tax revenue has grown in tandem with the expanding Gross Domestic Product (GDP), thus providing adequate resources to finance total Government spending.

sentences.speaker: Prof Hoon Hian Teck (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: It is likely that Singapore's economic take-off that caused our economy to grow faster than the world's technology leaders in those years, expanded the size of the economic pie and raised tax revenue at given tax rates to help pay for our national expenditure.

sentences.speaker: Prof Hoon Hian Teck (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: It is inevitable that with Singapore getting closer to the world technology frontier, growth must inevitably fall to a more moderate level that is typical among the advanced industrial economies.

sections.label: Enterprise Innovation Scheme
sections.summary: The Enterprise Innovation Scheme introduced in Budget 2023 will help businesses press on with innovation.

sentences.speaker: Prof Hoon Hian Teck (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In this regard, the Enterprise Innovation Scheme introduced in Budget 2023 will help businesses press on with innovation.

sections.label: SME co-investment fund
sections.summary: In Budget 2023, the SME co-investment fund was augmented to strengthen the enterprise financing ecosystem.

sentences.speaker: Prof Hoon Hian Teck (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: More successful early stage business ventures might then stimulate the supply of financing from venture capitalists.

sentences.speaker: Prof Hoon Hian Teck (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Therefore, in Budget 2023, with the augmenting, the SME co-investment fund, that helps to strengthen our enterprise financing ecosystem.

sections.label: Singapore Global Enterprises Initiative funding
sections.summary: Budget 2023 sets aside $1 billion to boost the Singapore Global Enterprises Initiative, adding support to internationalisation efforts.

sentences.speaker: Prof Hoon Hian Teck (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Setting aside $1 billion to boost the Singapore Global Enterprises Initiative in Budget 2023 adds further support to our internationalisation efforts.

sections.label: Government-paid paternity leave increase
sections.summary: Budget 2023 increases Government-paid paternity leave from two weeks to four weeks for eligible working fathers of Singaporean children.

sentences.speaker: Prof Hoon Hian Teck (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: That is how they spend their added income – investing in their children.

sentences.speaker: Prof Hoon Hian Teck (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: So, in that regard, increasing the Government-paid paternity leave from Budget 2023 from two weeks to four weeks for eligible working fathers of Singaporean children serves to widen the opportunity for children to benefit from their father's investment time in them.

sections.label: Ageing population and economic prosperity
sections.summary: Singapore will adopt a two-pronged approach to boost total fertility and manage a controlled flow of immigrants to keep the population from shrinking.

sentences.speaker: Prof Hoon Hian Teck (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Another reason is that the pace of innovation tends to slow down due to a decline in the supply of entrepreneurs as we have more people who are older in the population.

sentences.speaker: Prof Hoon Hian Teck (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: So, to generate economic prosperity in the mature phase, Singapore, I believe, will have to adopt a two-pronged approach, both to boost total fertility but at the same time to manage a controlled flow of immigrants to keep the population size from shrinking.

sections.label: Budget 2023 job holding measures
sections.summary: Budget 2023 introduces measures to uplift lower-wage workers' earnings and support reskilling displaced workers and matching them to new jobs.

sentences.speaker: Prof Hoon Hian Teck (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Budget 2023 affirms the centrality of job holding as it introduces measures to uplift the wage earnings of lower-wage workers and also provide support to reskill displaced workers and match them to new jobs.

sections.label: Workplace fatalities and safety period
sections.summary: Ely was one of 46 workplace fatalities in 2022, and MOM extended its six-month heightened safety period till May this year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Ely was one of 46 workplace fatalities in 2022 – the highest number since 2016, despite a heightened safety period imposed in September.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Additionally, the major injury rate per 100,000 workers has increased in the last few months from 16.8 to 18.7.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: In response to this, the Ministry of Manpower (MOM) has implemented a six-month heightened safety period since last September and has extended it till May this year.

sections.label: Workplace Safety and Health vision
sections.summary: The Workplace Safety and Health vision is to have workplace fatalities below one per 100,000 workers by 2028.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Our Workplace Safety and Health vision is to have workplace fatalities to be below one per 100,000 workers by 2028.

sections.label: Singapore tuition industry and PSLE stress
sections.summary: Tuition in Singapore is a billion-dollar industry with seven in 10 children enrolled, and the PSLE provides great stress.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Nevertheless, tuition in Singapore remains a billion-dollar industry, possibly a multi-billion-dollar industry, with seven out of every 10 children in Singapore enrolled in tuition, with the PSLE, in particular, providing a great element of stress.

sections.label: Doing away with PSLE
sections.summary: The speaker suggests considering doing away with the PSLE, citing Subject-based Banding's positive effects and a longer runway till 16.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: That would allow nearly every student to be assured secondary school entry in a school familiar to him or her.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: I would even suggest perhaps that we need to consider doing away with the PSLE altogether.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: That would give them a longer runway till 16 to prepare and allow late bloomers to catch up.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: We have already introduced Subject-based Banding (SBB) and see the positive effects of it to allow students to learn at their own pace and to remove possible stigma associated with certain labels.

sections.label: Removing PSLE to reduce pressure
sections.summary: Removing the PSLE would reduce pressure on students, and the suggestions could help Singapore develop students into citizens tackling tomorrow's problems.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Removing the PSLE would reduce the pressure on students.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Learning to mix with people from all walks of life is invaluable and wholesome and rich, and it carries into the working world.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: I humbly submit that, together, all these suggestions, along with the many others that I know MOE is considering, will be able to help Singapore continue its legacy of developing students who can grow into citizens who can tackle the problems of tomorrow.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: I believe we owe this to the residents we serve and in that way, we can build stronger solidarity to take Singapore forward.

sections.label: ChatGPT reaching 100 million users
sections.summary: ChatGPT took two months to reach 100 million users, compared with four years for Facebook, two for Instagram and one for Google.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
sentences.text: What took Facebook four years, Instagram, two, Google, one to achieve 100 million users, ChatGPT took two months.

sections.label: Nvidia AI chip market lead
sections.summary: Nvidia positioned its Pascal chip architecture for AI, holding 90% of the market for processing chips using training and machine learning.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
sentences.text: Nvidia took the lead as the company positioned its latest Pascal chip architecture as purpose-built for AI, holding 90% of the market for processing chips using training and machine learning today.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
sentences.text: Today, computational power used to train the largest AI models doubles every 3.4 months.

sections.label: Singapore AI readiness ranking
sections.summary: According to the Global AI Readiness Index, Singapore ranks second behind the US.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
sentences.text: According to the Global AI Readiness Index, Singapore ranks second behind the US.

sections.label: Global middle class graduates
sections.summary: The passage states there are 2.5 billion middle class people and gives 2020 university graduate numbers for China, India, the US and EU.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
sentences.text: Today, we have 2.5 billion people in the middle class.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
sentences.text: In 2020, China and India graduated over 90 million students from universities, with 2.7 million of them with degrees from science, engineering or technology.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
sentences.text: In the US and European Union (EU), 7.5 million students graduated from universities, mostly in business, healthcare, social science and law.

sections.label: Finnish face mask reserves
sections.summary: A Finnish report said this work let Finland stock up face masks in strategic reserves, readying them for COVID-19.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
sentences.text: According to one of the Finnish reports, it was this particular work that enabled Finland to stock up face mask as part of the strategic reserves which readied them for COVID-19.

sections.label: Continuing forefathers' work
sections.summary: The speaker says they continue their forefathers' work for a better future and supports the Budget.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
sentences.text: Today, we continue our work of our forefathers in building and fighting for a better future.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
sentences.text: We must not falter, not on our watch, not today, not tomorrow.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
sentences.text: For an impossible dream to a credible vision, we craft our reality for tomorrow.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
sentences.text: Majulah Singapura." Mr Speaker, I support the Budget.

sections.label: Eldercare Fund top-up
sections.summary: Deputy Prime Minister Wong announced a $500 million top-up to the Eldercare Fund for means-tested subsidies for seniors needing care.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Deputy Prime Minister Wong also announced that he will top up the Eldercare Fund by $500 million to support means-tested subsidies for seniors who need home-based, centre-based or institutional care.

sections.label: Hougang seniors medical subsidies
sections.summary: Hougang seniors told the speaker higher annual home values affected their medical subsidies, and he asks if the Government will review this.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Recently, some of the seniors in Hougang gave feedback to me that as the Government has increased the annual value of their homes, this has affected the ultimate medical subsidies they get.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Will the Government review the effect of the increase in the recent assessment of annual values on seniors' eligibility for medical subsidies?

sections.label: Working mother tax relief changes
sections.summary: From 1 January 2024 tax reliefs change to fixed sums per child, and the speaker asks if MOF calculated the scheme's net Budget effect.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Under the proposed changes announced during the Budget speech last week, the tax reliefs will be changed with effect from 1 January 2024 from a percentage of a working mother's income to a fixed sum for each of the first child, $8,000; second child, $10,000; third and subsequent child, $12,000.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Essentially, this affects working mothers having a child from January 2024 onwards.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: It remains to be seen whether and to what extent it may deter middle income earning working mothers from having children or more children under the scheme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Has the Ministry of Finance (MOF) calculated what is the net effect of this scheme on the Budget and whether it is one that significantly saves money?

sections.label: EV Charging Act and adoption
sections.summary: The EV Charging Act establishes charger standards, but the Government could do more to persuade switching, with EVs at 11.7% of 2022 cars.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: The passing of the Electric Vehicle (EV) Charging Act last year is welcomed, as it helps to establish clear technical and performance standards of all EV chargers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: However, I do feel that the Government can still do more to persuade people to make near-term plans to switch from internal combustion engine vehicles to electric vehicles, which is about just 11.7% of all cars registered in 2022.

sections.label: Public EV charging network limits
sections.summary: The public EV charging network of around 3,600 points is limited and inadequate for any significant immediate increase in EV numbers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: The current public network for EV charging of around 3,600 charging points is still limited and inadequate to support any significant immediate increase in EV numbers.

sections.label: 12,000 charging point deployment
sections.summary: The Government decided to focus on deploying 12,000 charging points, whose data may inform later adjustments.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: The Government has, therefore, decided to focus on the 12,000 charging point deployment and that the data from this deployment may inform the Government about the need for adjustment thereafter.

sections.label: EV Common Charger Grant details
sections.summary: The grant pays half of EV charger installation costs until 31 December 2023 or 2,000 chargers, with light goods vehicles at 28% adoption.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Still on the EV Common Charger Grant, I understand from the EV Charging Bill debate in November last year that the grant pays for half of the various costs involved in installing EV chargers and will be available until 31 December 2023, or when it has co-funded 2,000 chargers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Minister Iswaran said, in response to my queries at the EV Charging Bill debate in November, that the light goods vehicles segment saw the highest rate of EV adoption last year, at around 28%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Minister Iswaran also mentioned at the debate that the challenge is with the conversion of the so-called big trucks, with the trade-offs with propulsion and so on, and that hydrogen or related fuel types are being considered quite actively in that regard.

sections.label: Fast-ageing Singapore population
sections.summary: One in four Singaporeans will be 65 and above by 2030.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: First, our fast-ageing population, where one in four Singaporeans will be 65 and above by 2030.

sections.label: CPF rates for platform workers
sections.summary: Aligning platform workers' CPF contribution rates with regular employees would increase retirement security for riders, PHV and taxi drivers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: The Government's decision to align the CPF contribution rates of platform workers with those of regular employees, following the recommendations of the Advisory Committee on platform workers, would go some way to increase the retirement security for our delivery riders, private hire vehicle (PHV) drivers and taxi drivers.

sections.label: CPF top-ups and retirement savings
sections.summary: It asks how many self-employed persons voluntarily top up CPF accounts, noting eight in 10 active members turning 55 in 2027 are expected to have enough for the Basic Retirement Sum payout.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: How many SEPs voluntarily top up their Ordinary, Special and Retirement Accounts?

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: I note that eight in 10 active CPF members turning 55 in 2027, are expected to have enough savings to receive at least the CPF Basic Retirement Sum (BRS) payout.

sections.label: CPF contribution rates for older workers
sections.summary: It states the rationale for raising CPF contribution rates for workers aged 55 to 70 by 1% to 1.5%, but raises concern this may deter employers from hiring older workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Second, while I can see the rationale for increasing the CPF contribution rates for older workers between 55 and 70 years of age by 1% to 1.5%, I am concerned whether this would be an added disincentive for businesses and employers to hire older workers.

sections.label: CPF monthly salary ceiling increase
sections.summary: It states that the CPF monthly salary ceiling will rise progressively from $6,000 to $8,000 over four years, which has attracted debate on online forums.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Third, the progressive increase in the CPF monthly salary ceiling, from $6,000 to $8,000 over the next four years, has attracted some debate on online forums and earlier just now.

sections.label: CPF salary ceiling and interest rates
sections.summary: It asks whether mandating higher CPF contributions is necessary given workers' opportunity cost, notes added pressure on smaller firms, and says netizens queried why CPF interest rates have not increased.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Is it, therefore, necessary to mandate that such workers contribute a greater proportion of their wages into CPF, considering the opportunity cost to these workers?

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: I am also mindful that this raising of the salary ceiling is expected to add financial pressures on smaller firms who will need to pay increased employer contributions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Following the Deputy Prime Minister's explanation that the monthly salary ceiling has to go up in tandem with inflation, netizens have also queried why the interest rates on CPF funds have not been increased.

sections.label: CPF account interest rate reviews
sections.summary: It asks whether there is any intention to revise interest rates on the Ordinary, Special and MediSave Accounts in upcoming quarterly reviews.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Is there any intention to revise the applicable interest rates on the Ordinary, Special and MediSave Accounts in the upcoming quarterly reviews?

sections.label: History of CPF scheme
sections.summary: It states CPF began in 1955 as a home ownership savings scheme, and around the mid-1990s the Government rebalanced it for retirement income through the Special, MediSave and Retirement Accounts, housing withdrawal limits and the Minimum Sum Scheme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: In fact, when CPF was first started in 1955, it operated as a savings scheme for home ownership rather than a scheme for retirement income.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: It was only around the mid-1990s that the Government rebalanced the CPF system to boost cash savings for retirement, by putting in place the Special, MediSave and Retirement Accounts, limiting the amount of savings that can be withdrawn for housing and implementing the Minimum Sum Scheme.

sections.label: Singapore pension index ranking
sections.summary: Singapore's retirement income system ranked ninth out of 44 systems and top in Asia in the Mercer CFA Institute Global Pension Index 2022.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: In the Mercer CFA Institute Global Pension Index 2022, Singapore’s retirement income system was ranked ninth out of 44 systems that were studied, and the top in Asia based on the criteria of adequacy, sustainability and integrity.

sections.label: CPF minimum payout increase
sections.summary: The Budget announced an increase in the minimum CPF monthly payout from the Retirement Sum Scheme from $250 to $350.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: This is not an easy task given the many unpredictable variables when we look into the future.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: I welcome the Budget announcement that there will be an increase in the minimum CPF monthly payout from the Retirement Sum Scheme (RSS) from $250 to $350.

sections.label: Full Retirement Sum payouts
sections.summary: The 2023 Full Retirement Sum of $198,800 is based on the Household Expenditure Survey 2017/2018 and aims to provide $1,510 to $1,620 monthly for life.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: By way of comparison, the Full Retirement Sum of $198,800 in 2023 is calculated based on the Household Expenditure Survey 2017/2018 and aims to provide a monthly payout of $1,510 to $1,620 for life.

sections.label: Top ups for non-working women
sections.summary: Efforts need enhancing to help non-working women homemakers or caregivers get top ups by their husbands, especially at age 55.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: One, as mentioned above, we need to enhance the efforts to help the segment of non-working women homemakers or caregivers get top ups by their husbands especially at age 55 when the decision needs to be made.

sections.label: Escalating CPF LIFE plan inflation
sections.summary: The escalating CPF LIFE plan's payout increase rate was set at 2%, but long-term Singapore inflation may have risen slightly above 2%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: The additional CPF LIFE plan was to offer payouts that increase at a set percentage every year and the rate of increase of payouts was set at 2% for the escalating CPF LIFE plan.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: My concern is that the long-term inflation rate for Singapore may have risen to slightly above 2%.

sections.label: Support for Budget 2023
sections.summary: The speaker supports Budget 2023, which aims to address the longer-term future while providing transitory near-term support.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: On that note, I support Budget 2023 which aims to address our longer-term future while providing transitory near-term support.

sections.label: Jobs-Skills Integrators intermediaries
sections.summary: Deputy Prime Minister Wong announced Jobs-Skills Integrators, intermediaries working with industry, training and employment facilitation partners to optimise training and job placements.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: Deputy Prime Minister Wong announced the Jobs-Skills Integrators, an interesting concept of intermediaries that will work with industry, training and employment facilitation partners to optimise training and job placements.

sections.label: Senior employment support and training
sections.summary: Budget extends Senior Employability Credit and Part-time Re-employment Grant till 2025, and the Jobs-Skills Integrators pilot will be in sectors with more matured workers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: With inflation, businesses are facing increasing cost of doing business.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: I am glad that the Budget will provide additional support to employers to hire senior workers who wish to work with the extension of the Senior Employability Credit till 2025 and the Part-time Re-employment Grant till 2025.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: In our engagements with seniors and with employers, a key challenge that the employers and seniors highlighted was training and re-skilling of seniors for suitable jobs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: It is heartening to know that the pilot for the Jobs-Skills Integrators will be in sectors that have higher concentration of matured workers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: The learnings from the pilot on training and reskilling of seniors to the jobs in the pilot will be helpful in providing insights to improve the structure and delivery of training of seniors and better align the training to jobs for seniors in other sectors in future.

sections.label: Day and dementia care costs
sections.summary: Without subsidies, day care services cost $940 to $1,430 monthly, and dementia care services range from $1,260 to $1,575 monthly.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: Without subsidies, day care services can cost from $940 to $1,430 per month.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: Dementia care services range from $1,260 to $1,575 per month.

sections.label: CPF monthly income ceiling rise
sections.summary: Raising the CPF monthly income ceiling from $6,000 to $8,000 by 2026 means employees will get more from their employers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: The rise in CPF monthly income ceiling from $6,000 to $8,000 by 2026 will mean that employees will get more from their employers.

sections.label: Fixed dollar WMCR
sections.summary: The change to a fixed dollar for WMCR means working mothers claim the same tax relief for a child in the same child order.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: The change to a fixed dollar for WMCR will mean that working mothers will claim the same amount of tax relief for a child in the same child order.

sections.label: WMCR impact on higher-earning mothers
sections.summary: Working mothers earning around $4,500 a month will get significantly lower tax relief, prompting an appeal for a hybrid WMCR approach.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: Just taking a rough back of the envelope calculation, this would mean that the working mothers who are earning more, around $4,500 a month, or $54,000 per year, will get significantly lower tax relief compared to the current system.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: If the intent is to encourage and support working mothers to continue working after they have children, the appeal is to allow a hybrid approach of the new fixed WMCR amount for those earning less than $54,000 a year and the working mothers who have children after 1 January 2024 to continue to stay on this current system of using a percentage of earned income as there is already a $80,000 cap on the amount of personal income tax relief an individual can claim.

sections.label: Refreshed ITM for manufacturing clusters
sections.summary: Deputy Prime Minister Heng Swee Keat launched the refreshed ITM for five advanced manufacturing and trade clusters in October last year, aiming to uplift companies and create at least 13,400 new jobs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: For example, the hon Deputy Prime Minister Heng Swee Keat had launched the refreshed ITM for five advanced manufacturing and trade clusters, that has as its aim uplifting companies and creating at least 13,400 new jobs in October last year.

sections.label: Security association invited as observer
sections.summary: When a major committee for this cluster was convened, the Security Association Singapore was invited to attend not as a member but merely as an observer.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Curiously, when a major committee for this cluster was convened, my association, the Security Association Singapore (SAS), the lead trade association for the security sector, was invited to attend not as a member but merely as an observer.

sections.label: Association granted a seat
sections.summary: After some ding-donging, the association was granted a seat at the table.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: After some ding-donging, we were granted a seat at the table.

sections.label: SNEF should not replace trade associations
sections.summary: Where sectoral issues are discussed under a tripartite framework, SNEF should not replace the sectoral trade association and must not be seen as able to speak for individual industries.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In this regard, where there are sectoral issues to be discussed under a tripartite framework, SNEF should not replace the sectoral trade association and must not be seen by Government bodies as being able to speak on behalf of individual industries.

sections.label: LEAD Programme funding for TACs
sections.summary: The LEAD Programme funds projects by trade associations and chambers, with higher funding for multi-TAC projects, though funding is typically on a project basis.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The Government already has a very excellent Local Enterprise and Association Development (LEAD) Programme that funds projects undertaken by trade associations and chambers (TACs), that have certain objectives.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Funding is higher if the project involves more than one TAC, which I think is a very good arrangement because it encourages TACs to work together to enjoy economies of scale and to ensure a larger reach for each project.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: However, the funding available is typically on a project basis.

sections.label: Appointing TACs as programme partners
sections.summary: TACs could be strengthened by the Government appointing them as programme partners to administer certain schemes or grants.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: TACs could also be strengthened by the Government appointing them as programme partners to administer certain schemes or grants.

sections.label: MOM conciliation security employees
sections.summary: The matter went to MOM conciliation, and the union and company said conciliation resulted in a positive outcome.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The matter has now gone to MOM conciliation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This, in fact, is hot off the press – it is just from, I think, maybe two or so hours ago, an announcement, a statement from the Union of Security Employees and the company involved.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: It said that conciliation had resulted in a positive outcome and that the union understands it was the intent to right-size its workforce and to recognise the management's efforts to do so fairly.

sections.label: TAC representatives as experts
sections.summary: It is suggested that TAC representatives could be invited as experts in dispute resolution to explain industry situations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: My other suggestion, Sir, is, for precisely these types of dispute resolution, whether we could introduce a mechanism in which TAC representatives could be invited, where appropriate, as experts, to explain the situation in the industry or to perhaps provide more context and hue, to what are the considerations of companies in that sector.

sections.label: Union involving sectoral trade association
sections.summary: Another way to deal with disputes is for the union to involve the sectoral trade association informally from the start.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Another way to deal with such disputes is for the union to get the sectoral trade association involved from the very start, of course informally.

sections.label: Monitoring cohort progression and National Productivity Fund
sections.summary: It asks how the Government monitors cohort progression and notes the National Productivity Fund top-up and the old-age dependency ratio.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: How is the Government monitoring the cohort progression and targeting assistance to provide levelling up opportunities at milestone stages of their early work life?

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I like that the National Productivity Fund will be topped up substantially by $4 billion with an expanded scope to support investment promotion, besides productivity enhancements and continuing education and training.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Census 2020 showed that our old-age dependency ratio has increased from 13.5% in 2010 to 23.4% in 2020.

sections.label: Tracking local companies growth
sections.summary: It asks whether there is systematic tracking of local companies under the Singapore Global Enterprises initiative and SME Co-Investment Fund.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: In this aspect, do we have a systematic tracking of the growth of local companies under the $1 billion Singapore Global Enterprises initiative or the additional $150 million SME Co-Investment Fund, especially for the number of SMEs levelling up consistently across the years to be on track to become large local enterprises with annual group company revenue exceeding $100 million and with regional or even global footprints?

sections.label: Seniors healthcare costs and funds
sections.summary: It notes seniors' concerns over healthcare costs and looks forward to details on ElderCare Fund and MediFund top-ups.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Many of our seniors who seek assistance at my Meet-the-People Sessions often share their concerns of rising healthcare costs and their working adult children feel the pressure of supporting them while bringing up their own children.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I thus look forward to more details on the Government's plan to top up an additional $500 million for ElderCare Fund and $1.5 billion to MediFund to help lower-income seniors with their long-term healthcare needs.
