sections.label: Support for young couples and families
sections.summary: The Government is increasing the CPF Housing Grant, Baby Bonus Cash Gift and Child Development Account contributions to support first-time families and raise the low total fertility rate.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: We dedicated last year as "The Year of Celebrating SG Families" and there were many discussions on strengthening support for our young couples and families.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I am glad that the Government will be doing more by increasing the CPF Housing Grant by $30,000 for eligible first-time families purchasing 4-room or smaller resale flats and by $10,000 more for those purchasing 5-room or larger flats.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: In helping with the costs of having and raising children, I hope that initiatives such as the increase of Baby Bonus Cash Gift by $3,000 for all eligible Singaporean children and increase in contributions to the Child Development Account to offset preschool and healthcare expenses as well as support for more flexible work arrangements will have some effect in reversing our stubbornly low total fertility rate.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: According to the Marriage and Parenthood Survey 2021, 80% of young single respondents in that survey indicated that they intend to get married but only 50% of them are dating.

sections.label: Assistance measures for the elderly
sections.summary: A Jalan Kayu health club was set up, and the speaker supports Budget measures for seniors including the Senior Employment Credit, higher Retirement Sum Scheme payouts and ElderCare Fund and MediFund.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: In Jalan Kayu, our grassroots organisations have responded by setting up a new health club to help residents maintain good health through participating in a series of club activities.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Hence, I strongly support the suite of assistance measures for the elderly in the Budget, such as extending the Senior Employment Credit, increasing the minimum monthly payout under the Retirement Sum Scheme as well as additional ElderCare Fund and MediFund to help seniors cope with long-term medical care expenses.

sections.label: Helping workers upgrade skills
sections.summary: The Government will step up efforts to help workers upgrade and renew skills, and the speaker hopes Parliament will be told how effective these schemes are.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The Government will also step up efforts to help workers upgrade and renew their skills.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I hope that in the next few years, the Government will let the Parliament know how effective these schemes are in helping Singaporeans secure good jobs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I think helping promising SMEs expand and allow their employees to be trained continually will help Singaporeans secure better job opportunities.

sections.label: Support for Budget 2023
sections.summary: The speaker states support for Budget 2023.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: On this note, Speaker, I support Budget 2023.

sections.label: Cushioning the GST increase
sections.summary: The speaker welcomes enhancements to the permanent GSTV scheme and Assurance package to cushion the impact of the GST increase and fund healthcare spending and cost-of-living support.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: However, unlike those times, the current persistent inflation felt globally is fuelled with a tight labour market within Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Hence, I welcome the enhancements to the permanent GSTV scheme and Assurance package to cushion the impact of our much-needed GST increase so that we can maintain our commitments to fund impending healthcare spending and the one-off support measures to address the immediate cost-of-living challenges.

sections.label: One-off cost-of-living support
sections.summary: The speaker supports one-off schemes including the Cost-of-living special payment, Seniors Bonus, doubled U-save rebates and CDA top up, consistent with society supporting the less well-off.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: This is consistent with our values as a society and reinforces it with action where collectively as a society we support each other and the less well-off should receive more.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: I am supportive of tiding the current Cost-of-living challenges with one-off schemes such as the Cost-of-living special payment of $200 to $400, Seniors Bonus of $200 to $300, doubling of U-save rebates and CDA top up.

sections.label: Assurance Package cost and sustainability
sections.summary: The enhancement raises the Assurance Package from $6.6 billion to $9.6 billion, costing $3 billion, which the speaker says must be monitored and calibrated.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: The enhancement to the assurance package, both the one-off and the earlier versions will cost $3 billion and hence increases the total amount of the package from $6.6 billion to $9.6 billion which is more than the budget for Ministry of National Development (MND), or Ministry of Social and Family Development (MSF) and Ministry of Sustainability and the Environment (MSE) or MSE, Ministry of Culture, Community and Youth (MCCY), Ministry of Manpower (MOM) and Ministry of Communications and Information (MCI) combined!

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Hence, I believe that while this is necessary in the current environment, this is something we must closely monitor in future budgets and carefully calibrate the amount and qualifying conditions when the situation changes so as to avoid entrenching the sense of reliance on Government support as it is not fiscally sustainable in the long term.

sections.label: Investment promotion and National Productivity Fund
sections.summary: EDB attracted $22.5 billion in Fixed Asset Investment commitments in 2022, and the National Productivity Fund will be topped up with $4 billion and expanded to include investment promotion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: While EDB attracted a record high of $22.5 billion Fixed Asset Investment (FAI) commitments in 2022, which brings about good well-paying jobs into Singapore, with the headwinds and increasing competition, how can we create more non-tax incentives to enhance our business competitiveness to continue to attract foreign investment?

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Hence, I am encouraged to hear that the National Productivity Fund will be topped up with $4 billion and the scope will be expanded to include investment promotion as a supporting activity.

sections.label: Job-Skills Integrators pilot
sections.summary: The speaker asked about consolidating support into a worker-centric portal and welcomes piloting Job-Skills Integrators in a few industries as intermediaries.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: I asked whether this landscape can be consolidated into a worker-centric portal like "Support-Go-Where" which then provides the comprehensive support for the business and worker.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Hence, I am glad to hear that we will be piloting the Job-Skills Integrators in a few industries to be intermediaries who can work with industry, training, employment and facilitation partners to optimise training and job placement.

sections.label: PWM pilot duration and roll-out
sections.summary: The speaker asks how long the Progressive Wage Model pilot in Precision Engineering, Retail and Wholesale Trade will take and the expected pace of roll-out to other industries.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Similar to the PWM roll-out too, how long will the pilot in the Precision Engineering, Retail and Wholesale Trade sectors take and what will be the expected pace of roll-out to the other industries once the pilot industries are completed?

sections.label: Employment credit schemes success measures
sections.summary: With the extension of Senior Employment Credit and Part-Time Employment Grant and a new uplifting employment credit for ex-offenders, the speaker asks what measures success.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: With the extension of Senior Employment Credit, Part-Time Employment Grant and introducing uplifting employment credit for ex-offenders, what is the measure of success for these schemes?

sections.label: Assurance Package support and expenditure
sections.summary: The Assurance Package can give a middle-income family with 2 children and 2 seniors up to $8,000 this year, and enhancements raise its total from $6.6 billion to $9.6 billion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: The Assurance Package support network will be able to help many families, including the "sandwich class" families, where a middle-income family with 2 children and 2 seniors can receive support of up to $8,000 dollars this year The enhancements to the Assurance Package will increase its expenditure by $3 billion, thus increasing the total amount of the Assurance Package from $6.6 billion to $9.6 billion!

sections.label: Worker skills and productivity
sections.summary: The passage states a commitment to improve worker skills and productivity for real wage growth and asks about Jobs-Skills Integrators for skills and job placement.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: There is also a sustained commitment to improve the skills and productivity of workers so that the workers can see real wage growth while we also focus on inclusive growth so that everyone has employment opportunities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Therefore, I also would like to understand more about "Jobs-Skills Integrators" that will help employees improve their skills and facilitate job placement in growth industries.

sections.label: Luxury vehicle and property taxes
sections.summary: The passage states that tweaks to luxury vehicle ARF and buyer stamp duty for higher property values make the tax system fairer, more progressive, resilient and sustainable.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: The tweaks that were made on taxes on luxury vehicles ARF and buyer stamp duty for higher property values are in the right direction to make our tax system fairer, more progressive, resilient and sustainable.

sections.label: 2022 headline inflation
sections.summary: The passage states that headline inflation, the CPI of all items, is 6.1% in 2022, with transport, housing and utilities and food prices as main contributors.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Headline inflation, the CPI of all items, is 6.1% in 2022, with increase in transport, housing and utilities and food prices being main contributors.

sections.label: Past Reserves repayment commitment
sections.summary: The passage asks the Deputy Prime Minister to commit that money taken from Past Reserves will be put back at the earliest opportunity, if not at one go then in phases.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: I understand that it is always a tricky trade-off between spending for today, investing for the future and saving for the unexpected.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: But, could the Deputy Prime Minister give commitment that the money taken out of our Past Reserves will be put back at the earliest opportunity to do so, and if not at one go, at least in phases?

sections.label: BTO ballot for families
sections.summary: The passage states that the Government will refine the BTO scheme to give first-timer families with kids and young married couples aged 40 and below an additional ballot.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: The ability to secure a home gives our people, especially young couples, the confidence to build their families and in turn, reinforce their shared sense of destiny with Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Therefore, in this Budget, I am glad that the Government will refine the BTO scheme to give first-timer families with kids and young married couples aged 40 and below an additional ballot.

sections.label: Married Child Priority Scheme proportion
sections.summary: The passage asks whether the Government could consider increasing the proportion of flats set aside under the Married Child Priority Scheme in BTO projects at mature estates.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: While I understand the Government needs to make many considerations, such as ensuring a certain level of refreshing of the population in any precinct, could the Government consider increasing the proportion of flats set aside under the Married Child Priority Scheme (MCPS) in BTO projects at mature estates?

sections.label: Special needs places and teachers
sections.summary: The speaker hopes the Government will increase places and train more teachers for children with special needs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Still, I hope the Government will also do more to increase places and train more teachers for children with special needs.

sections.label: Porting subsidies for special circumstances
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether subsidies could be ported over for specific individuals in special circumstances.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: She felt torn between the ability to afford and settling for a centre that may not be suitable for her daughter.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Hence, I wonder if subsidies could be "ported" over for specific individuals in special circumstances like this?

sections.label: Support for anchor and partner operators
sections.summary: The speaker asks for better training and more resources so centres can accept more children with special needs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: But the process was disruptive for the child's learning and caused much heartache for the family.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Hence, could there be better training and more resources given to support all anchor operator and partner operator centres so that they can accept more children with special needs?

sections.label: Healthier SG and senior-friendly design
sections.summary: The speaker urges the Government to push for Healthier SG and make building plans and programmes friendly to seniors.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Entering the silver years can be a new beginning where there is life, people, new dreams and new adventures worth looking forward to every day.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Hence, I urge the Government to double up its efforts in pushing for a Healthier SG and ensure that building plans and programme offerings are by design friendly to seniors today and tomorrow.

sections.label: Married Child Priority Scheme quota
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether the Married Child Priority Scheme quota can be raised so more first-timers can secure homes near parents.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: First, to encourage the various generations in the family to take care of each other, can the Government raise the Married Child Priority Scheme (MCPS) quota so that more young first-timers can secure new homes close to their parents?

sections.label: Support, teachers and subsidised places
sections.summary: The speaker hopes the Government will increase teachers, provide more subsidised places and build a vibrant future for the elderly.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: It is only right to give them more support.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: I hope that the Government will increase the number of teachers in this area and provide more subsidised places.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Instead, this should be the beginning of a new chapter.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: I hope that the Government will continue to build a vibrant future for the elderly, promote Healthier SG and design activities, programmes or infrastructures with different age groups in mind.

sections.label: Budget builds on past efforts
sections.summary: The speaker says strong finances, willpower and give-and-take are needed, and sees this Budget as building on past efforts to take Singapore forward.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: To navigate around these challenges and steer Singapore forward, we will need strong financial muscles, solid willpower and a willingness to give and take.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Hence, notwithstanding my earlier points made, I see this Budget as one that builds on past efforts and one that will continue to take Singapore forward.

sections.label: Budget 2023 political statement
sections.summary: Budget 2023 is described as an inspired political statement spelling out duties for the rich, welfare for the poor and opportunities for all.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Budget 2023 is an inspired political statement that spells out duties for the rich, welfare for the poor and opportunities for all.

sections.label: Budget 2023 redistribution and free lunches
sections.summary: The passage says fiscal prudence means understanding prices, but Budget 2023's focus on redistribution shows free lunches exist for those who need them.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Indeed, it is still a principle of good fiscal prudence to understand the price of things.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: However, Budget 2023 with its high focus on redistribution, especially for those most vulnerable among us, shows that there are free lunches for those who need them.

sections.label: Singaporeans get more than paid
sections.summary: The passage states that in large sectors and biggest ticket items, most Singaporeans get far more than what they pay for.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: In large sectors of our economic life, in fact in the biggest ticket items, most Singaporeans get far more than what we pay for.

sections.label: Special COE category for super cars
sections.summary: The passage asks whether the Government can consider a special category for super cars so the COE market is competitive within that class.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Can the Government consider a special category for such "super cars" such that the COE market is competitive within this special class?

sections.label: Consolidated revenue account and NIRC
sections.summary: The passage states all Government revenues go into a consolidated revenue account, and since 1996 the NIRC accounts for most Government funding.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: The fourth financing principle of the Government outlined by Prof Lee is that all Government revenues go into a consolidated revenue account, which is that the Government does not tie revenue to specific expenditure items.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: This principle remains, but since 1996, one major change is that the Net Investment Returns Contribution (NIRC) today accounts for the majority of our Government funding.

sections.label: NTUC SME support requests
sections.summary: NTUC asks Government for enhanced support to offset costs, boost hiring and productivity for SMEs, including lower-interest loans and grant changes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: NTUC has called out to Government for enhanced support to offset these higher costs, to boost local hiring and productivity for our SMEs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: We ask Government to enhance the level of and the range of support to companies to offset high operating costs and manpower challenges, step up productivity and digitalisation initiatives.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Can the Government offer loans with lower interest rates and review eligibility criteria for grants, such as removing the 30% local shareholding requirement and to allow more SMEs to qualify for the Productivity Solutions Grant?

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Can we make upskilling a compulsory component in evaluating companies’ eligibility for tax relief, while providing complementary training grants for companies to send workers for training?

sections.label: COVID-19 expenditure audits
sections.summary: The speaker welcomes the response that over half of COVID-19 expenditure has been audited, with remaining audits expected by end of financial year 2024.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: These expenses are necessary to our successful navigation through the pandemic.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: I thus welcome Deputy Prime Minister’s response that over half of the COVID-19 expenditure have been audited, and the remaining audits are ongoing and are expected to be completed by the end of financial year 2024.

sections.label: Capital gains tax feasibility
sections.summary: The passage asks whether the Government is studying the feasibility of a capital gains tax for properties like HDB sold at a huge profit.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: First, is the Government studying the feasibility of a capital gains tax for properties like HDB that have been sold at a huge profit?

sections.label: UK and EU energy levies
sections.summary: The UK introduced an Energy Profits Levy at 35% and the EU imposes a 33% levy on fossil fuel firms' profits and revenues.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: For instance, the UK introduced the Energy Profits Levy currently at 35% and the EU imposes a 33% levy on fossil fuel firms’ profits and revenues made on rising electricity costs.

sections.label: Malaysia and Indonesia Sukuk
sections.summary: Malaysia leads the world in Sukuk issuance with US$80 billion in 2022, and Indonesia is third globally with US$22 billion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Regionally we are in the middle of powerhouses in this space, Malaysia is the country leading the world in Sukuk issuance year on year with US$80 billion in 2022 and Indonesia, third globally, with US$22 billion.

sections.label: BTO balloting system refinement
sections.summary: The speaker had suggested refining the BTO balloting system based on needs and types of applications, as applicants feel they compete with other communities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: However, they feel that they are still competing with many other applicants from the other communities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Thus, I had suggested in an earlier Parliamentary Question to further refine the BTO balloting system based on needs and types of applications.

sections.label: CDA use for baby essentials
sections.summary: The speaker proposes allowing CDA funds to be used for essential items like baby formula milk or diapers from authorised retailers, as allowable expenses are limited to certain education and healthcare costs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: However, the allowable expenses from the CDA is limited to certain education and healthcare costs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: I propose that the Government perhaps can consider allowing CDA to be used for essential items like baby formula milk or diapers; which can be bought from authorised retailers.

sections.label: Baby Bonus as CDC Voucher
sections.summary: The speaker suggests the Government consider allocating part of the Baby Bonus and BSG as a special CDC Voucher for households with young children of a certain age.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: In future, perhaps the Government can consider allocating a component of the Baby Bonus and BSG, in the form of a special CDC Voucher for households with young children of a certain age.

sections.label: Lower claim for working mothers
sections.summary: An analyst said it translates to a lower claim for any working mother with an annual earned income of about $54,000 or more.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: One analyst said it translates to a lower claim for any working mother with an annual earned income of about $54,000 or more.

sections.label: Budget support for young couples
sections.summary: The speaker categorises Budget support into housing aspirations, affordable child-raising and childcare support, but notes many feel it does not defray the COV issue of about $30,000 to $50,000 or more.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: I have broadly categorised this year's Budget support for young couples into three categories: (a) helping young Singaporeans to realise their housing aspirations; (b) ensuring that their journey of raising children remains affordable; and (c) increasing the availability and flexibility of more support for childcare.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: However, many feel that the support does not defray the existing issue, in that many young couples have opted out of resale flats as an option because the Cash Over Valuation (COV) component that is being insisted by many sellers in the open market.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: In many such situations, these amounts could end up in the region of about $30,000 to $50,000 or even more.

sections.label: WMCR tax relief reductions
sections.summary: The WMCR adjustment reduces tax reliefs for working mothers earning more than $4,500 monthly, with those earning $5,000 seeing a $1,000 reduction and those earning $8,000 a cut of about $6,400.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: While the WMCR adjustment comes as good news for working mothers in the lower-income group, for those earning more than $4,500 per month, this change will, in reality, reduce the amount of tax reliefs for them, with these reductions becoming more pronounced as their salary increases progressively.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Under the newly adjusted WMCR, those who earn about $5,000 per month would experience a reduction of $1,000 in tax relief while mothers with a monthly salary of $8,000 will see their tax reliefs drastically cut by about $6,400.

sections.label: Future-ready and family-friendly features
sections.summary: Enhancements such as complimentary 5G access, child safety features, family-friendly parking lots and more nursing and diaper changing facilities, supported by BCA's Accessibility Fund grant, are suggested.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: One example is to introduce enhancements that make homes future ready, whether by allowing complimentary access to 5G networks that makes it easier to work from home and installing various child safety features such as window guards and slip-resistant flooring.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: In recent years, apart from handicap parking lots, we have also begun to see more family-friendly parking lots in commercial malls.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: There has also been an increase in the availability of nursing and diaper changing facilities – thanks to BCA's Accessibility Fund grant.

sections.label: Changi Airport Special Assistance Lanes
sections.summary: ICA showcased Special Assistance Lanes at Changi Airport passenger halls for wheelchair users and family groups of up to four persons.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: ICA has recently showcased its Special Assistance Lanes at various passenger halls in Changi Airport to enable travellers using wheelchairs and family groups of up to four persons to enjoy the convenience of automated immigration clearance.

sections.label: Tripartite Standard Flexible Work Arrangements
sections.summary: Companies adopting the Tripartite Standard may need processes to ensure Flexible Work Arrangements are properly adopted and fair for employers and employees.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: For companies to adopt the Tripartite Standard, there may be a need to formulate processes to ensure that Flexible Work Arrangements (FWAs) are properly adopted by them and that the arrangements are fair for both employers and employees within each company.

sections.label: Median Gross Annual Income Growth
sections.summary: MOM data shows median gross annual income of full-time employed residents grew from $41,760 in 2012 to $56,160 in 2021.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Between 2012 and 2021, according to Ministry of Manpower's (MOM) data, the median gross annual income from work, including employer CPF contributions of full-time employed residents, grew from $41,760 to $56,160.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: In approximately the same time, data taken from the United States (US) census shows the median gross annual income from work to be at US$32,000 in 2012, compared to US$37,522 in 2021 – in Singapore, an increase of approximately $14,400 compared to $7,398 in the US.

sections.label: WHO Mental Disorder Work Data
sections.summary: WHO reports half the world's population works and 15% of working-age adults live with a mental disorder.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The WHO reports that half the world's population are currently in work and 15% of working-age adults live with a mental disorder.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Globally, 12 billion working days are lost every year to depression and anxiety alone.

sections.label: Senior Employment and Retirement Adequacy
sections.summary: The speaker welcomes Budget measures on senior employment, CPF increases and offsets, and asks what more can be done.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: For some, this is a way to keep actively engaged, but for others, it is a painful necessity to afford life.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I am glad that the measures in the Budget around the continued employment of seniors, should they choose, are centred around ensuring that companies are incentivised to compensate workers fairly, as well as retirement adequacy.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The CPF increase proposed in this Budget affects employer contributions as well and I understand that the Government has planned for an offset to assist companies in meeting this goal, as well as the senior employment credit.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: However, given that there are time limits to this, what more can be done on a societal level to prevent a drop off in hiring seniors when the credit and offset expires?

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: For example, for those who sell their homes and their parents' homes to consolidate into a multi-generational flat, I hope that we can relook the criteria of certain support schemes and caregiving subsidies dependent on flat type, to allow for elderly and their adult children to continue receiving help.

sections.label: Family Support and Gig Workers
sections.summary: The speaker hopes fathers play a more active role and the Government extends support to gig sector family members.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: With support such as increased paternity leave, enhancement to the Baby Bonus Cash Gift (BBCG) and the Child Development Account (CDA), I hope fathers can also play a more active role in taking care, educating and raising their children.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I also welcome the additional grants from the Government for those who want to buy resale flats.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: However, besides helping Singaporeans have a family and own their dream homes, I hope the Government would also extend its support to help family members working in the gig sector.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I was glad to hear the recent announcement to improve the financial security of platform workers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I have met gig workers who prefer cash income that they can receive promptly while they are still young, but upon reaching their 30s, they realised they did not have enough savings and CPF to buy a home.

sections.label: Work hours disconnection guidelines
sections.summary: Clear guidelines on work hours and designated times for disconnecting should be established.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: First, clear guidelines on work hours and designated times for disconnecting should be established.

sections.label: Zero-tolerance policy protocols
sections.summary: A zero-tolerance policy with clear protocols for handling such cases must be established.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: A zero-tolerance policy with clear protocols for handling such cases must be established.

sections.label: Compulsory preschool education
sections.summary: It may be time to mandate compulsory education for preschool.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Perhaps it is time that we mandate compulsory education for preschool.

sections.label: Skills training employment outcomes
sections.summary: This is a game-changer because not all skills training will translate into good employment outcomes.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: To me, this is a game-changer because not all skills training will translate into good employment outcomes.

sections.label: Flexi-work arrangements standard
sections.summary: The Government will introduce a voluntary Tripartite Standard on Flexi-Work Arrangements and make these arrangements more pervasive.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: I spoke previously about the need for employers to be more compassionate to our workers and recognise that individuals' priorities vary at different stages of their lives and that work and life are interdependent but increasingly intertwined.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Therefore, I am heartened that the Government will introduce the voluntary Tripartite Standard on Flexi-Work Arrangements and make these arrangements more pervasive.

sections.label: Mandatory work-safety committees
sections.summary: The Government should make it mandatory for every company to have a work-safety committee including a qualified union representative.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: However, more must be done to support workers to ensure workplace safety and health.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: I propose that the Government make it mandatory for every company to have a work-safety committee that includes a qualified union representative.

sections.label: KidSTART programme nationwide enhancement
sections.summary: The speaker welcomes the announcement to enhance the KidSTART programme nationwide.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: As for education, I welcome the announcement to enhance the KidSTART programme nationwide.

sections.label: Housing aspirations support measures
sections.summary: Supporting housing aspirations through additional ballots for BTO flat applications and increasing the CPF Housing Grant.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: First, by supporting housing aspirations through additional ballots for BTO flat applications and by increasing the CPF Housing Grant.

sections.label: CPF allocation ratio figures correction
sections.summary: The speaker corrects CPF allocation ratio figures, noting 2022 and 2023 changes and that quoted figures referenced the 2021 CPF Annual Report.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: In my speech, I mentioned at the part on retirement adequacy, that the contribution of a member's Ordinary Account drops to 21% when a member returns 36 years of age and is gradually reduced in five-year intervals to reach only 12% when a member returns 56.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: I got these figures from the latest CPF Annual Report which was tabled to Parliament on 27 June last year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: It has been brought to my attention that in 2022 and 2023, the CPF allocation ratios actually have changed slightly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: So, I think it is important that I put that on the record, and that the figures that I quoted were in reference to the Annual Report of the CPF of 2021.

sections.label: Nurse workloads and pay increases
sections.summary: Nurses face heavy workloads and long shifts, attrition has risen, and MOH pay increases are welcomed but do not go far enough.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Their workloads are heavy, their shifts are long and they get little time to rest.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: So many nurses have shared with me that nurses are resigning en masse.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Attrition rates have gone up and I know the Government is aware of this problem.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I am glad that the Ministry of Health (MOH) has been reviewing the salaries and allowances of nurses and also announced a 2022 Nurse Special Payment package.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: These increases in pay are welcomed but do not go far enough.

sections.label: Nurses missing toilet and rest breaks
sections.summary: A nurse said toilet breaks are often missed, and 90% of surveyed nurses said working during rest breaks is common.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: One nurse shared with me, "It is not uncommon for nurses to not have enough time to have toilet breaks because of the amount of things that come to us during the shift." Of the nurses I surveyed, 90% shared that it is common for them to have to continue working during their rest break.

sections.label: Nurses hindered by administrative duties
sections.summary: Nearly 80% of surveyed nurses felt unable to focus on clinical care because administrative duties were much heavier than necessary.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Of the nurses surveyed, nearly 80% felt that they were not able to focus on clinical care because of administrative duties that were much heavier than necessary.

sections.label: Nurses customer service burden
sections.summary: Seventy-seven percent of surveyed nurses felt they cannot focus on clinical work because too much time goes to customer service.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Seventy-seven percent of nurses surveyed felt that they cannot focus on clinical work because too much time is spent on providing customer service to patients.

sections.label: Care Ambassadors helpful to nurses
sections.summary: More than 70% of nurses said Care Ambassadors were helpful or very helpful in letting them focus on clinical care.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: More than 70% of nurses shared that the Care Ambassadors were helpful or very helpful in allowing them to focus on clinical care for patients.

sections.label: Nurse rest and support staff
sections.summary: The passage asks whether mandating protected rest time and hiring more support staff can help nurses rest more.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Can we help our nurses have more rest by mandating protected rest time between shifts, providing strong protections for rest time during shifts, and hiring more support staff, including ancillary care staff and Patient Care Officers?

sections.label: Nurse overtime, workload and inflation
sections.summary: A nurse describes being marked down for not being a team player, and the passage notes nurses' workload and Singapore's 2022 inflation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Another nurse told me, "We are called back for overtime when staff is down, when we don’t go to work because we are tired, the management counts the number of times and mentions it in our appraisal for not being a team player and marks us down for it.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: People leave because they see no end to this dark tunnel." I hope MOH can provide nurses with some light at the end of this dark tunnel and look into the three recommendations I have raised on their behalf.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: As we transition out of the pandemic, the workload of nurses has not eased and they continue to be on the frontline when it comes to our health.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Singapore has registered a steady increase in core inflation throughout 2022, hitting almost a 14-year high in September with 5.3%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Overall, core inflation for 2022 stood at 4.1% and headline inflation was at 6.1% – a significant increase from 2021 and before.

sections.label: Singapore family offices count
sections.summary: At the end of 2022, Singapore had almost 700 family offices.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: At the end of 2022, Singapore had almost 700 family offices.

sections.label: Paid paternity leave extension
sections.summary: The Government has recommended extending paid paternity leave from the mandated two weeks to four weeks.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: As a father, I am heartened to learn that the Government has recommended an extension of paid paternity leave from the current mandated two weeks to four weeks.

sections.label: Paid childcare leave suggestion
sections.summary: The speaker suggests the Government consider providing at least three days of paid childcare leave for parents until children turn 18.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: As such, I would like to suggest that the Government consider providing at least three days of paid childcare leave for parents until their children turn 18 years old.

sections.label: Percentage-based resale flat grant
sections.summary: The speaker hopes the Government will consider a percentage-based grant based on resale flat price for families with children buying in mature estates.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: In this regard, it is not just about getting support from their elderly parents to help with their own young children, but rather also to facilitating and supporting, helping their own elderly parents while managing their own young children.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I hope that the Government will consider granting families with children a percentage-based grant based on the price of a resale flat if they wish to purchase a flat in a matured estate as opposed to an absolute grant as presently structured.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: A percentage-based grant will make resale housing more relatively affordable in mature estates and care more accessible for such families.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: It also would be a more equitable distribution of grants that are needs-based rather than one that is a standard amount.

sections.label: Crisis preparation and SGSecure training
sections.summary: The speaker supports scaling up Total Defence table-top exercises and urges more funding and training in life-saving skills under SGSecure.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Thus, I was heartened to learn about the pilot Total Defence Community Table-top exercises where residents presented their suggestions on how to prepare for future crises.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: I support the decision to scale up this exercise so that more communities can participate as part of the SGSecure programme.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Indeed, during times of peace, we need to practise and ensure that we are familiar with the essentials of coping in emergencies and life-saving skills.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: I urge the Government to enhance the funding, support and resource allocation for crisis preparation among its agencies and on the ground.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: It is time for SGSecure to go beyond the threat of terrorism and to mean more than "Run, Hide, Tell" to our people.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: I hope that we can gather at least half of all Singaporeans to step forward to be trained in first aid, CPR, basic firefighting and other critical life-saving skills and to start training our younger generation in all these skills as well.

sections.label: Guarding against societal fault lines
sections.summary: As a multiracial, multi-religious society, Singapore needs to be extra vigilant against attempts to strike at societal fault lines and destabilise the community.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: (In English): As a multiracial, multi-religious society, we need to be extra vigilant to guard against attempts to strike at the fault lines in our society and to destabilise our community.

sections.label: Enterprise Innovation Scheme and funding
sections.summary: The speaker welcomes the new Enterprise Innovation Scheme and other funding, and asks about the scheme's aims or KPIs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The new Enterprise Innovation Scheme, the top-up of $150 million for the SME Co-Investment Fund, $4 billion for the National Productivity Fund and $1 billion for the Singapore Global Enterprises initiative, amongst others, are greatly welcomed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: What are the aims or KPIs of the new Enterprise Innovation Scheme?

sections.label: Separate COE category for vans
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether commercial vans can have a separate COE category and grants so end consumers pay less.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The COE of a van is $87,000 currently.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Can we have a separate category for commercial vans and provide grants to these companies so that end consumers can pay lesser?

sections.label: Electric commercial vehicle costs
sections.summary: Electric commercial vehicles may cost more upfront but offer lower operating costs, reduced maintenance and environmental benefits.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Generally, electric commercial vehicles may have a higher upfront cost compared to their conventional counterparts, but they offer lower operating costs, reduced maintenance expenses and environmental benefits.

sections.label: ITE teaching assistant recruitment
sections.summary: The advisor of the Union of ITE Training Staff hopes MOE gives more resources to ITEs to recruit teaching assistants.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: I declare that I am the advisor of the Union of ITE Training Staff.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: I hope the Ministry of Education (MOE) can give more resources to the ITEs so that it can start to recruit teaching assistants like what the other public schools are already doing currently.

sections.label: Private sector mental health tapping
sections.summary: It asks whether MOE can tap private sector psychiatrists and psychologists so deserving students receive diagnosis quickly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Like Healthier SG, can MOE tap on private sector psychiatrists and psychologists so that deserving students can receive diagnosis quickly?

sections.label: Funding for disability programmes
sections.summary: More funding is required to develop specialised programmes for students with disabilities including autism, visual and hearing impairments, and learning difficulties.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: More funding is required to develop more specialised programmes for students with different disabilities, including autism, visual and hearing impairments, and learning difficulties.

sections.label: Singapore regional comparison scan
sections.summary: Singapore had Southeast Asia's highest median age in 2022 and higher business operating costs, yet remains top choice for higher value-added manufacturing.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: While doing a regional comparison scan, Singapore has the highest median age of any population in Southeast Asia in 2022.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: We stand at 42.1 years old, compared to Indonesia at 29.4 years, Malaysia at 30.4 years, Cambodia at 25.6 years and Vietnam at 31.9 years old.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Our monthly average operating costs to do business is approximately 64% to 76% higher than other countries in the ASEAN region.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Despite the high costs, Singapore is still the top choice for companies with higher value-added manufacturing with complex processes and automation requirements.

sections.label: Enterprise SG grants well-being survey
sections.summary: The motion proposed Enterprise SG grants include a survey on employees' well-being before and after project implementation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: In my Adjournment Motion on strengthening mental wellness at the workplace, I proposed that Enterprise SG grants, such as the Enterprise Development Grant (EDG) and the Productivity Solutions Grant (PSG) include a survey on employees' well-being before and after the implementation of the project to measure potential improvements on employees' wellness, in addition to employee's value add gains.

sections.label: Temperature and sea level rise
sections.summary: From 1980 to 2020 annual mean temperature rose from 26.9°C to 28.0°C, and Straits of Singapore mean sea level rose 1.2 to 1.7 millimetres yearly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: From 1980 to 2020, the annual mean temperature has increased from 26.9°C to 28.0°C.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: The mean sea level in the Straits of Singapore has also increased at the rate of 1.2 millimetres to 1.7 millimetres per year.

sections.label: Climate adaptation economic opportunity
sections.summary: Climate change adaptation is a tremendous economic opportunity for Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Climate change adaptation is a tremendous economic opportunity for Singaporeans.

sections.label: Fiscal implications and foreigner taxes
sections.summary: There are fiscal implications, tax revenue is needed from an aging tax base, and foreigners contribute taxes while receiving few social benefits.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: There are fiscal implications, we continue to need tax revenue from an aging tax base.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Also, it is important to note that foreigners do not just compliment Singaporeans in the workforce but also contribute to taxes and do not receive much of the social benefits.

sections.label: Targeted manpower measures for growth
sections.summary: The speaker calls on the Government to review targeted manpower measures for key growth areas, better jobs, higher wages and a greener economy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Sectors still recovering from the pandemic need help to transform while those that are ready should be enabled to seize emerging opportunities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: I, hence, call on the Government to continue to review more targeted manpower measures vis-à-vis key growth areas that bolster our economy with better jobs, higher wages and support our transition to a greener economy.

sections.label: Competitiveness, carbon accounting, climate resilience
sections.summary: Singapore should stay competitive in customer experience and human capital management, equip enterprises to account for carbon, and build a climate resilient nation as exportable value.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: First, that we remain competitive and relevant by constantly benchmarking on two key areas, customer experience and human capital management, and equipping our enterprises with the ability to account for carbon as more MNEs and regional economic blocks are factoring supply chain carbon footprint in their purchasing evaluations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: And second, that we continue to build a climate resilient nation and turning this into a new exportable economic value.

sections.label: Resale grant price spiral
sections.summary: The resale grant will push up resale flat demand and prices, later requiring further resale grant increases feeding a continuous price spiral.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The resale grant will push up demand for resale flats and therefore, increase resale prices, which would later necessitate a further increase in resale grants feeding into a continuous price spiral.

sections.label: Corporate tax rates by profit level
sections.summary: MOF data shows companies with profits of $200,000 to $10 million paid 8% to 9% tax for YA2018 to YA2021, while larger companies paid less.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Based on MOF's reply to my Parliamentary Question (PQ) on corporate taxes paid by companies of different profit levels, it is seen that for YA2018 to YA2021, companies earning profits before tax of between $200,000 and $10 million paid on average 8% to 9% of their profits as taxes.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Companies earning between $10 million and $100 million in profits paid on average 5.1% of their profits as tax.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: For companies earning between $100 million and $1 billion in profits, 2.8%.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: To illustrate, a company making $2 million in profits pays 9% of its profits as taxes.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: This is 10 times the rate of a company that makes $2 billion in profits, that is, 1,000 times the profit.

sections.label: Higher tax on top companies
sections.summary: If companies earning above $1 billion paid 3% instead of 0.9%, about $5 billion more revenue would be raised yearly.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: For example, if companies earning above $1 billion in profits pay just 3% of their profits as taxes instead of the current 0.9%, the additional revenue raised would be about $5 billion per year!

sections.label: Using corporate tax revenue
sections.summary: Higher corporate tax revenue could lower business cost and cost of living, offsetting the higher effective tax rate and keeping Singapore attractive.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: With higher corporate tax revenue, we can use that to lower business cost and cost of living to offset the higher effective tax rate thereby making Singapore still an attractive investment destination and provide relief to Singaporeans.

sections.label: EWMC worker outreach
sections.summary: The #EWMC aims to reach at least 20,000 workers through dialogues, focus group discussions and surveys to hear views on work.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: The #EWMC aims to reach out to at least 20,000 workers through dialogues, focus group discussions and surveys to hear their views around work and to refresh NTUC's compact with workers.

sections.label: Company Training Committees update
sections.summary: NTUC introduced CTCs in 2019, supported by a $70 million CTC Grant, and around 1,200 CTCs have been formed with 17 projects approved.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: And that is why in 2019, NTUC introduced the concept of Company Training Committees (CTCs) between our unions and employers to support business transformation that can lead to company-initiated training and skills upgrading for workers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: We are thankful for Government's support with the $70 million CTC Grant which commenced in August last year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: To date, I am happy to update that we had formed around 1,200 CTCs, approved 17 companies' CTC Grant projects, with many more applications being processed, as we speak.

sections.label: RPS applies for CTC Grant
sections.summary: After positive CTC outcomes, RPS applied for the CTC Grant and committed to wage increments for impacted local workers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: Having experienced the positive outcomes from CTC for both business and workers, RPS has applied for the CTC Grant with a commitment to give wage increment for the impacted local workers.

sections.label: Jobs-Skills Integrators pilot initiative
sections.summary: The Labour Movement welcomes Deputy Prime Minister Lawrence Wong's announcement of the Jobs-Skills Integrators pilot, starting with three sectors.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: The Labour Movement is therefore pleased to hear Deputy Prime Minister Lawrence Wong announce the Jobs-Skills Integrators pilot initiative, which will commence with three sectors.

sections.label: SkillsFuture Career Transition Programme made long-term
sections.summary: The SkillsFuture Career Transition Programme, implemented in April 2022, becomes a long-term programme replacing the pandemic-era SGUnited Skills and Mid-Career Pathways programmes.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: The SkillsFuture Career Transition Programme (SCTP) implemented in April 2022 is a good example.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: I am glad that the Government has decided to make this a long-term programme in replacement of the SGUnited Skills Programme (SGUS) and the SGUnited Mid-Career Pathways Programme which were implemented during the pandemic.

sections.label: Landscape workers' wage increases
sections.summary: Landscape workers' wages rose 3.5% per annum from $1,300 in 2016 to $1,650 in 2022, and will continue increasing to about $2,385 in 2028.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: For example, the landscape workers have moved up by 3.5% per annum from $1,300 in 2016 to $1,650 in 2022, more than twice the median wage increase of 1.4%.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: These wages will continue increasing, till about $2,385 in 2028.

sections.label: Minimum wage and Living Wage proposals
sections.summary: Different minimum wage proposals exist: $1,300 by the Workers' Party and $1,800 by PSP, while the LQS rose $100 yearly from 2017 until COVID-19.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: As for the level of minimum wage or "Living Wage" that has been proposed, we note that there have been different proposals: $1,300 by Workers' Party; $1,800 by PSP this year, which is $300 more than the $1,500 that they proposed in 2021.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: The LQS is a stable methodology and until COVID-19, the LQS has been increased $100 each year from 2017.

sections.label: PWM wage-raising track record
sections.summary: PWM has a proven track record of raising wages without the risk of job losses.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: PWM has a proven track record of raising wages without the risk of job losses.

sections.label: NTUC $70 million government grant
sections.summary: NTUC is pleased to receive a $70 million government grant to continue developing training and placement support for local workers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: NTUC is pleased to receive a $70 million grant from the Government for us to continue to develop the training and placement support ecosystem for local workers and provide more employment assistance and support for them.

sections.label: Energy Efficiency Grant extension
sections.summary: Deputy Prime Minister Lawrence Wong mentioned the extension of the Energy Efficiency Grant, which eligible businesses would welcome.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: Deputy Prime Minister Lawrence Wong mentioned the extension of the Energy Efficiency Grant which would be welcome by eligible businesses.

sections.label: Three Fs approach
sections.summary: A threefold approach of financial support, facilitated employment and training, and fair access to PME roles is needed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: To do so, we need a threefold approach, what I call the "three Fs": first, financial support for displaced workers to cushion them and their families in the short term as they actively search for new employment; second, facilitated employment and training to upgrade workers and help them seize opportunities in the new economy; third, fair access to PME roles to allow our local PMEs to compete with foreign PMEs, regardless of age, on a level playing field and boost local PMEs' employment outcomes and strengthen the Singaporean Core.

sections.label: Survey on unemployment support
sections.summary: An April 2021 online survey of 500 respondents found almost 80% supported unemployment support, mostly to cover basic needs during job search.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: There are understandably concerns that with unemployment support, workers will remain unemployed for longer periods, making it harder for them to re-enter employment and causing a strain on Government resources.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: However, in an online survey with 500 respondents conducted in April 2021 as part of the PME Taskforce's work, almost 80% supported the introduction of unemployment support, with most citing that it would help workers cover their basic needs during their job search.

sections.label: COVID-19 Recovery Grant
sections.summary: MSF introduced the COVID-19 Recovery Grant to give temporary financial support to workers who lost jobs, took no-pay leave or lost income.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: At the height of the pandemic, the Ministry of Social and Family Development (MSF) introduced the COVID-19 Recovery Grant (CRG) to provide temporary financial support to workers who experienced involuntary job loss, no-pay leave or income loss.

sections.label: Self-Employed Persons Income Relief Scheme
sections.summary: SIRS was introduced to help freelancers and the self-employed tide through the first year of the pandemic, up to $1,000 monthly for up to nine months.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: In the same vein, we introduced the Self-Employed Persons Income Relief Scheme (SIRS) to help freelancers and the self-employed to tide through the first year of the pandemic for up to $1,000 per month and up to nine months.

sections.label: Mature PMEs job confidence survey
sections.summary: An April 2021 online survey of 1,000 respondents found only 58% of mature PMEs were confident of getting a job with their current skills.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: In another online survey with 1,000 respondents conducted in April 2021 as part of the PME Taskforce work, only 58% of mature PMEs were confident in getting a job with their current skills and capabilities.

sections.label: SkillsFuture Credits for career coaching
sections.summary: The speaker asks SkillsFuture Singapore to consider extending SkillsFuture Credits to engage personal career counselling, advisory and coaching services, currently limited to selected workforce segments.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: Beyond larger establishments like NTUC’s e2i and Workforce Singapore, there are numerous private sector career coaches that individuals can tap on.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: I therefore ask for SkillsFuture Singapore to consider extending the usage of SkillsFuture Credits to engage personal career counselling and advisory as well as coaching services as these are currently limited to selected segments of the workforce.

sections.label: Penalties for discriminatory companies
sections.summary: The speaker says a penalty framework should exist for egregious companies with discriminatory practices, and hopes the upcoming Workplace Fairness legislation balances protecting the local workforce and business needs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: For the small proportion of egregious companies with discriminatory practices, there should be a penalty framework in place to bring them to task.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: I hope that the upcoming Workplace Fairness legislation will strike a good balance between protecting our local workforce and managing business needs.

sections.label: NTUC three Fs for workers
sections.summary: The speaker says a threefold approach of financial support, facilitated employment and training, and fair access to PME roles is needed, and NTUC will champion these for all workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: To support our workers as they navigate these uncertainties, we need a threefold approach with the "three Fs" of financial support to cushion displaced workers in the short-term, facilitated employment and training, as well as fair access to PME roles.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: We at NTUC will continue to champion these for all workers, so that every worker can secure better wages, welfare and work prospects because every worker matters.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: The strong tripartite bond between Government, employers and the labour movement has been our secret weapon for many years and will continue to do so as we transition into a new and prosperous future.

sections.label: Fiscal balance deficit projections
sections.summary: Using the Government's accounting conventions, the fiscal balance will result in a deficit of -0.3% of income in the fiscal year just past and a projected deficit of -0.1% for the year to come.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: To be clear, the fiscal balance, using the Government’s accounting conventions, will result in a deficit of -0.3% of income in the fiscal year just past and there is projected deficit of -0.1% for the year to come.

sections.label: Permanent voucher scheme increase
sections.summary: The Budget's announcement that the permanent voucher scheme would be increased restores the Government's original promise of offset years and exceeds it with an additional $3 billion boost to the Assurance Package.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The Budget’s announcement that the permanent voucher scheme would be increased restores the Government’s original promise of offset years, and in fact, if anything, exceeds it with an additional $3 billion boost to the Assurance Package.

sections.label: Revenue measures and CPF ceiling
sections.summary: The measures add a cumulative $600 million to revenue, and the Budget raises the CPF ceiling from $6,000 to $8,000.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: While they do not go as far as we would like, they do add a cumulative $600 million to revenue.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The Budget also raises the CPF ceiling from $6,000 to $8,000.

sections.label: Public R&D spending comparison
sections.summary: It cited 0.7% spending versus about 1% in Denmark, Sweden and Switzerland, and a $4 billion Productivity Fund injection to bring Singapore's public share closer to comparators.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: It cited the spending of 0.7% relative to Denmark, Sweden and Switzerland, all of which spend around 1%.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: This Budget, to be clear, will inject the Productivity Fund with another $4 billion, which should bring our public share closer to that of our comparators.

sections.label: Enterprise Innovation Scheme tax deductions
sections.summary: It states that increased public R&D spending plus tax incentives for private R&D would help, and this Budget introduces an Enterprise Innovation Scheme to enhance tax deductions for innovation activities.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Here is where a combination of increased spending in public R&D, coupled with strong tax incentives to foster private R&D would come in.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: This Budget introduces an Enterprise Innovation Scheme meant to enhance tax deductions for innovation-related activities in Singapore.

sections.label: SME Co-Investment Fund injection
sections.summary: Minister Wong announced an additional $150 million injection into the SME Co-Investment Fund.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Minister Wong also announced that the SME Co-Investment Fund would enjoy an additional injection of $150 million.

sections.label: Domestic top-up tax 2025
sections.summary: Minister Wong shared that a domestic top-up tax would likely be implemented in Singapore in 2025 to comply.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Minister Wong shared that to comply, a domestic top-up tax would likely be implemented here in 2025.

sections.label: Workers' Party redundancy insurance proposal
sections.summary: It describes the Workers' Party redundancy insurance proposal: about six months coverage, 40% of last-drawn salary payout, deliberately conservative for financial sustainability.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The Workers' Party longstanding proposal, raised at least since our 2015 manifesto, on redundancy insurance is broadly consistent with these principles.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Our suggested coverage duration of about six months is lower than the one year or more common to schemes in other countries, albeit still in line with our nation's lower than average unemployment spells of about two months.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The proposed payout of 40% of the last-drawn salary is about average but still on the low side for advanced economies.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: We were deliberately conservative here to ensure financial sustainability.

sections.label: Government contribution to redundancy pool
sections.summary: It states this part amounts to workers taking care of other workers, and the Government should contribute regularly to the pool via a special-purpose development fund to keep the tripartite social contract intact.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: This part amounts to workers taking care of other workers.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: But to ensure that the tripartite nature of the social contract remains intact, the Government should also step in and contribute regularly to this pool in the form of a special-purpose development fund.

sections.label: CDC vouchers at supermarkets
sections.summary: The $300 CDC vouchers can now be used at participating supermarkets, in addition to heartland merchants and hawkers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: For example, the $300 CDC vouchers can now be used at participating supermarkets in addition to heartland merchants and hawkers.

sections.label: Retrenchment and abuse examples
sections.summary: Eagle Services Asia carried out an unfair retrenchment in July 2020, and security officers were often subjected to verbal and physical abuse.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: One such example that I would like to highlight is the unfair retrenchment exercise carried out by Eagle Services Asia in July 2020.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Our union leaders from the aerospace and aviation industry conducted a secret ballot to sanction legal industrial action against the company.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Another example is concerning our security officers who were often subjected to verbal and physical abuse.

sections.label: NTUC administered SIRS
sections.summary: NTUC volunteered to administer the Self-Employed Persons Income Relief Scheme, where eligible self-employed persons received $9,000 from the Government.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Besides standing up for the rights of our workers, how many of us can recall when NTUC volunteered to administer the Self-Employed Persons Income Relief Scheme (SIRS) for self-employed personnel (SEP), where eligible individuals received a total of $9,000 from the Government?

sections.label: Worker 4.0 vision
sections.summary: Under Secretary-General Ng Chee Meng's guidance, they envision the model Worker 4.0.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Under the guidance of our Secretary-General, brother Ng Chee Meng, we envision the model, Worker 4.0.

sections.label: Company Training Committees and Jobs-Skills Integrators
sections.summary: NTUC embarks on Company Training Committees to achieve its mission, and the Jobs-Skills Integrators model is welcomed and supported.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: To achieve this mission, NTUC embarks on what we called the Company Training Committees (CTCs).

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The recently announced Jobs-Skills Integrators model is one that I really welcome and wholeheartedly support.

sections.label: Support for families and disabilities
sections.summary: The passage asks whether support for bigger HDB households, families with hidden disabilities, extended childcare leave and larger families will be reviewed or extended.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Will the support for those living in bigger HDB houses be reviewed based on income and number of dependants instead of just annual value of the house?

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: While there are measures to support people with physical disabilities, will the Government also support families who have children with hidden disabilities like Autism Spectrum Disorder and Attention-deficit Hyperactivity Disorder as these are equally challenging scenarios?

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Will the extended childcare leave of two days per year be extended to parents who have children above 12 years of age, perhaps till the child completes secondary school?

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Will there be additional support for families with more than two children and with their parents staying with them?

sections.label: Support for self-employed persons
sections.summary: Calls to expand training allowances, develop skills frameworks, and consider GST rebates and cost co-sharing for SEPs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: First, expand the training allowance for self-sponsored trainees to include SEPs so that they can afford a few days off to upskill.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
