sentences.text: Thirdly, develop skills frameworks for SEPs and crafts and trades-based professions, such as for photographers, videographers, plumbers, mechanics, and incorporating apprenticeship programmes into such training frameworks with Government support In the area of levelling business costs due to the small size of the businesses, most SEPs are unlikely to grow to a scale where they can become GST-registered, but they face the full impact of GST increments on their business cost and may not enjoy the Government support given to businesses as they are freelancers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Consider providing GST rebates for SEPs who are not GST registered to buffer the increase in cost.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: For taxi and private hire drivers specifically, we should consider the co-sharing of GSTs by SEPs with their operators and platforms.

sections.label: Women outside the labour force
sections.summary: MOM notes 260,000 women of employment age are outside the labour force, citing home caregiving and housework as top reasons.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: MOM has noted that there are 260,000 women of employment age currently remaining outside of the labour force and their immense potential to power our economy and industries cannot be underestimated.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: It was interesting to note that according to MOM's annual labour for statistics, the two most cited reasons why women are not in the workforce are: one, home caregiving duties; and two, housework.

sections.label: Flexible work and job redesign
sections.summary: Bringing women back to work requires workplaces to evolve through flexible work arrangements and job redesign, adopted during the pandemic.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: To allow our women back into the workplace, the workplace will need to evolve and the prolific adoption of flexible work arrangements (FWAs) and the consequent need to job redesign was a silver lining that happened in the dark cloudy days of the pandemic.

sections.label: Sectors facing acute hurdles
sections.summary: Lists retail, food services, healthcare, manufacturing, wellness, security, cleaning and landscaping as sectors where hurdles are more acutely felt.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Some of these sectors where hurdles are more acutely felt include the retail, food services, healthcare, manufacturing, wellness, security, cleaning and landscaping sectors.

sections.label: Job redesign support package
sections.summary: The Labour Movement can work with the Government on grants, road maps and specialised consultancies through a job redesign support package.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: For this, the Labour Movement can work with the Government on a combination of grant support, road maps and specialised consultancies through a job redesign support package.

sections.label: Crafts and trades programmes
sections.summary: Crafts and trade programmes with various partners saw doubled women returners, and calls for continued Government and employer support.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: To this end, crafts and trade programmes promoted include tailoring and dressmaking with TaF.tc; confinement and infant nanny care with NannyPro; plumbing with the Singapore Plumbing Society (SPS) and logistics with the Singapore Logistics Association.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: We have seen some good progress on this front, for instance, we saw a doubling of women returners joining the tailoring programme from 2021 to 2022.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: And for the same time period, a doubling of women joined us in the SPS networks.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: In this light, we call for the Government to continue the support of our women returner programmes, in particular, for the popular trades and crafts person programmes, and for employers to join hands with NTUC in designing and adopting positive returnship programmes.

sections.label: Graduate salary gap widening
sections.summary: From 2016 to 2021, the university-polytechnic graduate gap grew by $200 and the university-ITE gap by $300.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: From 2016 to 2021, the gap between university and polytechnic graduates increased by $200; and $300 between university and ITE graduates.

sections.label: Median salary by education
sections.summary: Singaporeans in their 20s and 30s with university or post-graduate degrees earn a median $4,200, over double those with secondary or lower and ITE qualifications.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: For example, the median salary for Singaporeans in their 20s and 30s with a university or post-graduate degree is $4,200.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: This is more than double of that earned by those with only secondary or lower education and ITE qualifications.

sections.label: Tax incentives for companies
sections.summary: Government can provide more resources, perhaps tax incentives, to companies keen to support such a social compact.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Government can provide more resources, perhaps in the form of tax incentives, to companies keen to support such a social compact.

sections.label: 2022 graduate employment survey findings
sections.summary: The 2022 Joint Autonomous Universities Graduate Employment Survey found more graduates jobless six months after school than in 2021, though wages are higher if employed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: The 2022 Joint Autonomous Universities Graduate Employment Survey found that, compared to 2021, more graduates remained jobless six months after leaving school, though wages are higher if they land a job.

sections.label: Interest in overseas work
sections.summary: Sixty-six percent indicated their interest in working overseas.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Sixty-six percent indicated their interest in working overseas.

sections.label: Support for strategic industry placements
sections.summary: Government can consider targeted support like co-funding remuneration and relocation incentives for placements in strategic industries short on talent.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: The Government can look into providing targeted support such as co-funding remuneration and relocation incentives where the placements are done in strategic industries, where Singapore is short on talent.

sections.label: Subsidies for second diplomas
sections.summary: A speaker says failing to switch earlier can harm careers and urges graduated subsidies and loans for second diplomas and degrees for younger Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: A failure to switch decisively earlier can result in downstream difficulties to seize growth opportunities or even going down the wrong career trajectory.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: I encourage the Government to consider offering graduated subsidies and loans for second diplomas and degrees to younger Singaporeans.

sections.label: Budget 2023 housing support
sections.summary: Budget 2023 gives extra support to first-time flat buyers, including an additional BTO ballot for families and young couples and a higher CPF Housing Grant for resale flats.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
sentences.text: Budget 2023 has provided additional support to this specific group of Singaporeans and the support ranges from an additional Build-To-Order (BTO) flat ballot for families with children and young married couples aged 40 and below who are buying a flat for the first time, as well as an increase in the CPF Housing Grant for first-timer families purchasing resale flats.

sections.label: Shorter Waiting Time flats
sections.summary: Minister Desmond Lee announced HDB would resume building 2,000 to 3,000 Shorter Waiting Time flats per year by 2025.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
sentences.text: Minister Desmond Lee also announced in early this month that HDB would resume building 2,000 to 3,000 such Shorter Waiting Time (SWT) flats per year by 2025.

sections.label: Enhanced baby bonus increase
sections.summary: Couples will receive an extra $3,000 under the enhanced baby bonus for eligible Singaporean children, raised from $8,000 to $11,000.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
sentences.text: But for those who do choose to have children, easing the financial burden always helps.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
sentences.text: I am glad that couples will be given an extra $3,000 as part of the enhanced baby bonus for eligible Singaporean children and now raising from $8,000 to $11,000.

sections.label: Support for elderly living alone
sections.summary: The share of seniors over 65 living alone or with other seniors rose from 29% in 2010 to 41% in 2020, and the speaker suggests making the Silver Housing Bonus more attractive.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
sentences.text: In Singapore, Mr Speaker, Sir, the percentage of seniors over the age of 65 living alone or with other seniors increased from 29% in 2010 to 41% in 2020.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
sentences.text: Apart from the concerns arising from the elderly living alone, it is clear that if this trend continues, the elderly will require smaller living spaces which are easier to maintain.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
sentences.text: I suggest that the Silver Housing Bonus scheme, which enables the elderly to supplement their retirement income if they downsize to a three-room or smaller flat, could be made more attractive to improve the take-up rate.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
sentences.text: The cash bonus, which is currently up to $30,000 for seniors 55 years and above, could be doubled.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
sentences.text: At the same time, the resale levy, if any, could be halved.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
sentences.text: For the elderly who move to a smaller flat and want to stay within close proximity to their families to promote family bonding even while maintaining a separate household, HDB could provide additional subsidies.

sections.label: Budget 2023 expenditure comparison
sections.summary: Budget 2023's expenditure is 2.6% lower than last year but higher than pre-pandemic Budgets.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Notably, Budget 2023’s expenditure is 2.6% lower than last year, although higher than prior Budgets before the pandemic.

sections.label: MTI economic growth forecast
sections.summary: MTI forecasted economic growth between 0.5% and 2.5%, down from 3.6% last year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The Ministry of Trade and Industry (MTI) forecasted our economic growth to be between 0.5% and 2.5%, down from 3.6% last year.

sections.label: Budget 2023 SME support
sections.summary: Budget 2023 factored help for SMEs, including extending the Enterprise Financing Scheme and Energy Efficiency Grant and Jobs-Skills Integrators.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Nonetheless, while much has been said about more support being provided to families, individuals and vulnerable households, I do note that Budget 2023 has also factored some help for our SMEs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I welcome the extension of the Enterprise Financing Scheme and the Energy Efficiency Grant and am also glad to see the Government attempt a new initiative to address the jobs and skills mismatch through the Jobs-Skills Integrators.

sections.label: SME ESG capabilities measures
sections.summary: Budget 2023 retains measures such as the Resource Efficiency Grant for Energy and Enterprise Sustainability Programme by Enterprise Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Little has been said in this Budget specifically about SMEs strengthening capabilities in Environment, Social and Governance (ESG).

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I am glad that Budget 2023 retains existing measures such as the Resource Efficiency Grant for Energy as well as the Enterprise Sustainability Programme by Enterprise Singapore.

sections.label: Scam cases and losses
sections.summary: 2022 saw record cases and $660 million lost, close to $1.3 billion lost in two years, and $146 million saved by Anti-Scam Command.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Year 2022 saw both record cases and losses of $660 million.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: So far, close to $1.3 billion has been lost to scams in the past two years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: A further $146 million would have been lost last year had our Anti-Scam Command not partnered banks and telecommunications companies or telcos for a swift intervention.

sections.label: Neighbour noise mediation enforcement
sections.summary: Dr William Wan echoed the need for more legal teeth for attending mediation and enforcing agreements between quarrelling neighbours.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: In my recent engagement with Dr William Wan, Chairperson of the Community Advisory Panel on Neighbourhood Noise, he too echoed the need for more legal teeth to make attending mediation and to strengthen the enforcement of agreements between quarrelling neighbours.

sections.label: Application download count
sections.summary: Since its launch, the application has been downloaded more than 130,000 times.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: Since its launch, the application has been downloaded more than 130,000 times.

sections.label: Unit pricing on items
sections.summary: Unit pricing is displayed on over 1,200 items, including groceries and beauty products.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: Today, we have unit pricing displayed on over 1,200 items, including groceries and beauty products.

sections.label: NTUC FairPrice customer savings
sections.summary: Last year, NTUC FairPrice gave customers more than $11.5 million in savings through discount schemes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: Last year, NTUC FairPrice provided customers with more than $11.5 million in savings through various discount schemes.

sections.label: Workers who died after work
sections.summary: Last year, 46 workers did not make it home after work.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: Last year, a total of 46 workers did not make it home after work.

sections.label: Safety ambassadors and workplace injuries
sections.summary: Over 1,000 union leaders were trained as safety ambassadors, and rail operations workplace injuries fell by almost 30% from January to June 2022 versus 2021.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: We have trained more than 1,000 union leaders as safety ambassadors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: We have also worked with our unionised companies, through the Company Training Committees (CTCs), to redesign jobs and to redesign the work environment to improve workplace safety.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: If we compare the data from January to June 2022 versus the same period in 2021, the number of workplace injuries for rail operations fell by almost 30%.

sections.label: Workers co-mingling on lorries
sections.summary: The speaker urges the Government to end allowing workers to co-mingle with goods and heavy equipment at the rear deck of lorries.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: Beyond the dangers at the workplace, I have also raised numerous times, in and outside of this House, on the importance of ensuring the safety of our workers’ transportation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: I strongly urge the Government to end the practice of allowing workers to co-mingle with goods and heavy equipment at the rear deck of lorries.

sections.label: Tripartite Advisory on mental well-being
sections.summary: MOM, NTUC and SNEF published the Tripartite Advisory on Mental Well-being at the Workplace in November 2020, including recommendations on after-hours work communication.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: MOM, together with NTUC and the Singapore National Employers Federation (SNEF), subsequently published the Tripartite Advisory on Mental Well-being at the Workplace in November 2020 which included recommendations on after-hours work communication.

sections.label: Active Ageing Centres review
sections.summary: DPM Wong proposed reviewing AACs' operating model; the speaker wants more AACs, assisted living, overnight respite and palliative care for seniors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: In his Budget speech, Deputy Prime Minister Wong proposed reviewing the operating model of Active Ageing Centres (AACs).

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: Last year, during the Healthier SG debate, I shared with the House how Kebun Baru provides assisted living services through a piloting a communal centre at Block 115 in Kebun Baru.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: I feel that we must increase the number of AACs substantively and ensure they are thriving communities for seniors, offering loving care, connecting them to doctors, nurses, social workers and assisted living providers, while encouraging our seniors to stay positive and healthy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: Additionally, we should consider providing overnight respite and palliative care for seniors living nearby.

sections.label: DBS CPF property loan
sections.summary: DBS and CPF launched a loan pledging houses, topping up CPF; the speaker suggests mandating more banks, higher loan quantum, insurance changes and default LPA.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: Recently, DBS and CPF started a collaboration where DBS would offer a loan using houses as a pledge at an affordable interest rate.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: Seniors do not have to pay back the loan until the house is sold many years down the road.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: This loan is used to then top up their CPF account, allowing them to earn higher interest rates and enjoy higher monthly payouts from CPF.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: I hope that MAS can perhaps consider mandating more banks to join this programme and also increase the loan quantum, which would benefit more residents from private housing estates.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: We should also think about changing our insurance regulations, permitting seniors to withdraw a portion of their life insurance for aged care.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: This reduces the amount due to their estate and it lowers returns, but this is a fair trade-off to allow our seniors to fund these services using their insurance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: Also, we can consider introducing a default Lasting Power of Attorney (LPA) for seniors who have lost mental capacity and do not have an LPA in place.

sections.label: Workfare Income Supplement enhancements
sections.summary: WIS enhancements took effect from January 2023, including raising the qualifying monthly income cap from $2,300 to $2,500.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Workfare Income Supplement (WIS) enhancements took effect from January 2023, including a rise in qualifying monthly income cap from $2,300 to $2,500.

sections.label: Expanding payouts for dependants
sections.summary: The speaker calls on the Government to expand eligibility and increase payouts for those with dependants, phasing out benefits gradually and indexing payouts to cost of living.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: In this regard, I would like to take the opportunity to call on the Government to expand the eligibility criteria and increase payouts for those with dependants to cover more middle-income workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: To improve liquidity further, we recommend the Government phase out benefits more gradually by changing cash or CPF ratio and index pay-outs to cost of living.

sections.label: Progressive Wage Models coverage
sections.summary: The PWMs will cover around 135,000 full-time lower-wage workers, and with Progressive Wages measures would benefit up to 94% of lower-wage workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Combined, the PWMs will cover around 135,000 full-time lower-wage workers, which represent almost half of the total number of lower-wage workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Together with Progressive Wages measures recommended by the Tripartite Workgroup on Lower-Wage Workers such as the expanded Local Qualifying Salary (LQS) and the Progressive Wage Mark (PW Mark) accreditation, this would benefit up to 94% of lower-wage workers.

sections.label: Lift and Escalator PWM salary
sections.summary: Under the Lift and Escalator PWM, his salary is expected to increase from $2,600 to $3,820 by 2028.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Under the Lift and Escalator PWM, his salary is expected to increase from $2,600 to $3,820 by 2028.

sections.label: Local Qualifying Salary requirement
sections.summary: From September 2022, firms hiring foreign workers had to pay all local employees at least the LQS of $1,400 per FTE or relevant Progressive Wages.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: From September 2022 onwards, firms hiring foreign workers needed to pay all local employees at least the LQS, which is currently at $1,400 for one Full-Time Equivalent (FTE), or relevant Progressive Wages, which are higher.

sections.label: Annual review of LQS
sections.summary: NTUC called on the Government to annually review the LQS so wages keep pace with wage convergence targets for lower-wage workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: At NTUC, we are cognizant that efforts to help lower-wage workers is a long-term strategy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Therefore, I would like to call on the Government to annually review the LQS to ensure that wages keep pace with wage convergence targets for our lower-wage workers.

sections.label: Retirement age and CPF changes
sections.summary: In July 2022 the retirement and re-employment ages rose to 63 and 68, and in January 2023 CPF rates for workers above 55 were raised in a tiered structure.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: In July 2022, the Government raised the Statutory Retirement Age and the Re-employment Age ceiling by a year each, to 63 and 68 respectively.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: In January 2023, the Government adjusted upwards the CPF contribution rates for senior workers above the age of 55 according to a tiered structure.

sections.label: Tripartite Committee 2030 goals
sections.summary: The Tripartite Committee set 2030 goals of retirement age 65, re-employment age 70, and equalising CPF rates for ages 55 to 60.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: The goals set out under the Tripartite Committee for the older workers set 2030 as the year where we would aim to achieve the outcomes.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: We aim to reach the statutory retirement age of 65 by then and the re-employment age ceiling of 70 by then and for equalising the CPF contribution rates for those aged 55 to 60 with those of younger cohorts while strengthening the rates for who those who are older in a tiered manner.

sections.label: Senior worker employment rates
sections.summary: Employment rates for senior workers aged 55 and above reached new highs during the pandemic, rising for those aged 55 to 64 and 65 to 69.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: The Employment Rate for senior workers aged 55 and above has reached new highs in the course of this pandemic period.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: So, for example, for those who are aged 55 to 64, it went up by three points, from 67.6% in 2019 to 70.6% in 2022; and for those aged 65 to 69, it went up to 47.5%, which is an increase of 2.9% from the year 2019.

sections.label: Part-time re-employment grant
sections.summary: The speaker supported extending the Part-time Re-employment Grant to 2025, having argued in 2019 that part-time work unlocks a latent workforce.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: In the 2019 Budget debate, I had argued that enabling proper part-time work options is an important way to unlock a latent workforce among Singaporeans so that more middle-aged or older Singaporeans who may have had to leave work can instead stay in work or return to work, and companies in turn will be able to retain more good workers and have a bigger local workforce to meet their varied needs.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: I therefore also welcome and support the Government’s extension of the Part-time Re-employment Grant to 2025.

sections.label: CPF contribution ceiling raise
sections.summary: Raising the CPF contribution ceiling from $6,000 to $8,000 is supported by the speaker.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: The raising of the CPF contribution ceiling from $6,000 to $8,000 does that and I fully support it.

sections.label: Retirement adequacy for age cohorts
sections.summary: DPM Wong noted different age cohorts face different retirement saving prospects and pledged varied government help beyond Budget steps.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: Deputy Prime Minister Wong was frank in noting that different age cohorts of workers will likely face different prospects and challenges in saving for an adequate retirement.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: I am heartened by his pledge that Government will formulate different ways to help Singaporeans achieve basic retirement adequacy and is actively studying ways to do so, beyond the steps that have already been taken such as those in this Budget.

sections.label: Workplace Fairness interim report
sections.summary: MOM recently released the interim report of the Tripartite Committee on Workplace Fairness.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: MOM recently released the interim report of the Tripartite Committee on Workplace Fairness.

sections.label: Tracking household food insecurity
sections.summary: NGO studies found up to one in 10 Singapore households food insecure, and MSF does not specifically track this.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Various NGO-commissioned studies have recently found that up to one in 10 Singapore households are food insecure.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: I note from a reply to a Parliamentary Question (PQ) I posed last year that the Ministry for Social and Family Development (MSF) does not specifically track the food insecurity experienced by our vulnerable households, although there are various workgroups and initiatives to provide support.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: I believe that there is room for our Ministries and agencies to specifically track this issue to measure the effectiveness of our support schemes.

sections.label: Baby bonus for single mothers
sections.summary: Single unmarried mothers are left out of enhanced baby bonus tweaks and singles are more affected by rising rents.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: In particular, single unmarried mothers are left out of the enhanced baby bonus tweaks and our singles are generally more adversely affected by increasing rental prices.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: It therefore behoves us as a society to ask that our enhanced baby bonus and parenthood policies are extended equally to all parents.

sections.label: Singles flats and fiscal impact
sections.summary: Children of single unmarried mothers are under 1,000 yearly, so equalising support has small fiscal impact; singles should buy new flats at 28.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Moreover, children born to single unmarried mothers only form under 1,000 of live births each year, according to 2021 statistics and thus the fiscal impact each year of the equalising of financial support to children of single unwed parents would not be significant.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Changing demographics that lead to more singles across all age groups is also why we believe that singles should be allowed to purchase new flats from the age of 28, rather than the current 35.

sections.label: Youth mental health symptoms
sections.summary: The speaker urges urgent study of mental health, citing a study finding one in three youths internalise and one in six externalise symptoms, with up to 75% never seeking help.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: I hope that we look into this phenomenon urgently here in Singapore, as I believe more must be done to understand the scale of the problem, its effects on the well-being – physical and mental – of our people.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: I was also alarmed to read that the initial report from the Singapore Youth Epidemiology and Resilience Study found that one in three youths in Singapore report internalising mental health symptoms like sadness, anxiety and loneliness, and that one in six externalise symptoms such as hyper-activity and aggression.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: An estimated up to 75% of these people never seek professional help or treatment.

sections.label: Singapore worker stress survey
sections.summary: Mercer's 2022 survey found 85% of Singapore workers felt at risk of burn-out and one in five felt de-energised at work, double the Asia average.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Just on the work front, Mercer's 2022 Global Talent Trends Survey found that Singapore workers were highly stressed, with 85% feeling at risk of burn-out, and one in five are feeling de-energised at work, double that of the Asia average.

sections.label: Singapore sleep-deprived city ranking
sections.summary: Singapore ranked third out of 43 in a survey of sleep-deprived cities.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Singapore often ranks high amongst the echelons of sleep-deprived cities, coming in third out of 43 in one of these latest surveys.

sections.label: Teenagers' average sleep hours
sections.summary: Duke-NUH found teenagers sleep an average of 6.5 hours a night rather than the recommended eight hours.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Duke-NUH recently found that teenagers are only sleeping an average of 6.5 hours a night rather than the recommended eight hours for optimal development and functioning.

sections.label: Later school start times proposal
sections.summary: The speaker hopes to implement later school start times, a proposal previously put forward by Assoc Prof Jamus Lim.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: My colleague, Assoc Prof Jamus Lim, previously put forward this proposal and I hope we seriously move to implement later school start times, particularly when less of the workforce is now required to be at the workplace at 9 am.

sections.label: Property prices and cooling measures
sections.summary: The speaker says property prices must be kept in check and agrees with the Government's cooling measures to curb demand while supply is increased.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: We need to keep our property prices in check.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I agree with the Government's cooling measures to curb the demand while striving to pump up the supply which was interrupted by the COVID-19 pandemic.

sections.label: HDB flat and EC supply
sections.summary: Asks whether HDB can raise flat supply from 25,000 to 50,000 yearly for two years and double new EC supply.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Will HDB be able to increase the supply of HDB flats from the current 25,000 to even more, such as 50,000 per year for the next two years?

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Would HDB consider doubling the number of new Executive Condominiums (ECs) supply?

sections.label: Progressive Wage Marking inclusion
sections.summary: Says the changes strengthen the social compact and echoes NTUC's call to include skilled tradesmen like plumbers and electricians in the PWM.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: These changes are steps towards strengthening our social compact to be a more inclusive society that values both cognitive and technical skills.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I echo the appeals of NTUC's Secretary-General for skilled essential tradesmen like plumbers, electricians and air-conditioning technicians to be included in the PWM too.

sections.label: Sail Milestone Achievement Programme
sections.summary: SailMAP encourages Singaporeans to take up sea-going careers, with tripartite partners contributing up to $50,000 per local seafarer at key milestones.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The Sail Milestone Achievement Programme (SailMAP) is an excellent initiative to encourage Singaporeans to take up a sea-going career.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Tripartite partners contribute up to $50,000 to each local seafarer through this programme when he achieves key milestones in his career.

sections.label: Singaporean seafarers in maritime hub
sections.summary: States a core group of Singaporeans is important for supply chains in vital sectors, and their wages should be uplifted to retain them.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: As an international maritime hub, it is important to have a core group of Singaporeans to keep the supply chain going in these vital sectors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: We should also be looking at uplifting their wages to retain more of these seafarers as they form the backbone of the team navigating our local waters and we should provide a holistic career for them.

sections.label: GST Voucher and Assurance Package
sections.summary: The enhanced GST Voucher Scheme and Assurance Package direct more help to low- and middle-income groups, seniors, and employers hiring seniors, ex-offenders and persons with disabilities.

sentences.speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The enhanced permanent GST Voucher Scheme and Assurance Package ensure that more help is directed to the low- and middle-income to overcome the effects of high inflation and GST.

sentences.speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Seniors will be receiving higher CPF payouts and eldercare subsidies.

sentences.speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Employers hiring senior workers, ex-offenders and persons with disabilities will be given wage subsidies.

sections.label: Fixed sum tax relief suggestion
sections.summary: Suggests keeping the fixed sum as the minimum tax relief for a mother while retaining percentage-based calculation up to $80,000.

sentences.speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Can I suggest instead that we keep the fixed sum as the minimum amount of tax relief a mother should get while retaining the percentage-based calculation to a maximum of $80,000?

sections.label: Budget 2023 help and redistribution
sections.summary: Budget 2023 directs help to those who need it most, does not forget vulnerable groups, and redistributes wealth so those with more give more.

sentences.speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Budget 2023 ensures that help is directed to those that need it the most.

sentences.speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: It does not forget the vulnerable groups and redistributes the wealth so that those who have more will give more.

sentences.speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: However, I still believe that this Budget is leading Singapore in the correct direction and I fervently hope that future Budgets will carry the same spirit and intent.

sections.label: New BTO estate amenity tenders
sections.summary: In new BTO estates, tenders for childcare and other amenities only go out after residents start moving in, causing a demand and supply problem.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: For new BTO estates, the tender for childcare and other amenities only go out after residents start moving in, resulting in a demand and supply problem.

sections.label: Infant and childcare in new estates
sections.summary: Infant care and childcare facilities are critical in new estates and should be ready as residents move in.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: Infant care and childcare facilities are critical in new estates and should be ready as residents move in.

sections.label: Cost of raising a child
sections.summary: People said that if the cost of raising a child could be managed on a single income and/or with flexi-work arrangements, it would be more appealing.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: Many people I spoke to shared that if the cost of raising a child could be managed on a single income and/or with flexi-work arrangements, it would then be a much more appealing prospect.

sections.label: Work-from-home default ended
sections.summary: It is about 14 months since work-from-home was no longer made default on 1 January 2022.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: Incidentally, it is about 14 months since work-from-home is no longer made default on 1 January 2022.

sections.label: New fertility centre in eastern region
sections.summary: A new fertility centre in the eastern region is proposed to serve BTO estates in Tampines, Sengkang and Punggol.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: My final point is, can we consider opening a new fertility centre in the eastern region to serve our BTO estates in Tampines, Sengkang and Punggol?

sections.label: Co-funding for fertility and kidney care
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether portable co-funding, private-public collaboration and reduced pre-implantation genetic screening costs can help sub-fertile couples and chronic kidney and nursing home patients.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: Can we look at portable co-funding like portable subsidy in Agency for Integrated Care (AIC) for chronic kidney and nursing homes?

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: Could we have private-public collaboration to help sub-fertile couples after they have had two failed in vitro fertilisation (IVF) attempts in public hospitals?

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: Can we use co-funding or reduce the cost of pre-implantation genetic screening (PGS) so that couples who have suffered miscarriages can have a better chance if they wish to choose a better grade embryo for transfer?

sections.label: Budget schemes for seniors
sections.summary: The Budget announced new or enhanced schemes for seniors, including the Cost-of-Living Seniors' Bonus, Senior Employment Credit extension, higher CPF contribution rates, and top-ups for the ElderCare Fund and Community Silver Trust.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Many new or enhanced schemes to provide for seniors were announced during this Budget.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: They ranged from financial incentives such as the Cost-of-Living Seniors’ Bonus, to promoting senior employability and retirement adequacy through the Senior Employment Credit extension and increment of CPF contribution rates, to top-ups for the ElderCare Fund and the Community Silver Trust.

sections.label: Few incentives for sandwiched families
sections.summary: The speaker says this Budget contains few incentives specifically targeted at helping sandwiched families.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Unfortunately, I do not see many incentives in this Budget that are specifically targeted towards helping sandwiched families.

sections.label: Aid for shrinking caregiver group
sections.summary: Smaller families and smaller old age support ratios mean greater awareness and more aid are needed for this shrinking group of eventual caregivers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Our population is trending towards smaller families and smaller old age support ratios.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: This means greater awareness and more aid for this shrinking group of eventual caregivers is needed.

sections.label: Training coordinators for caregivers
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether AIC or the Regional Health Systems can train a team of coordinators to journey with caregivers, especially lower-income ones, from start to end.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Can AIC or the Regional Health Systems (RHS) be more targeted and consider training a team of coordinators who can journey with our caregivers, especially those from the lower-income families, from start to end?

sections.label: Innovating assistance for family caregivers
sections.summary: If family is the first pillar of support, better forms of assistance must be innovated for people living out that value, especially the less financially privileged.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: If we believe family should be the first pillar of support, we must keep innovating better forms of assistance for the very people who are trying their utmost to live out that value, especially those who are less financially privileged.

sections.label: Valuing seniors, not burden
sections.summary: The passage calls for shifting the mental model of society to value seniors' contributions and reframe their silver years as a different phase of life.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: For one, we must shift our mental model of our society from viewing seniors as a burden.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Instead, we should value our seniors' contributions and reframe their silver years as a different phase of life.

sections.label: Business survey key challenges
sections.summary: The Singapore Business Federation's latest national business survey highlighted key challenges: increased overall business costs, manpower availability and retention, and cost pressures including raw material, energy, manpower and rental costs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The Singapore Business Federation's latest national business survey highlighted that the key challenges faced by businesses in Singapore were an increased and overall business costs, the availability and retention of manpower and the main cost pressures include raw material cost, energy cost, manpower cost and rental cost.

sections.label: Low-rent options for SMEs
sections.summary: The passage proposes JTC expand its industrial space market share and offer more low-rent options to SMEs, and HDB offer lower rent commercial spaces by ballot to stimulate micro-businesses and entrepreneurship in the heartlands.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: To achieve this, JTC could expand its market share for industrial space and offer more low-rent options to SMEs and the Housing Development Board (HDB) could also offer lower rent commercial spaces allocated by ballot to stimulate micro-businesses and entrepreneurship in the heartlands.

sections.label: Rider accidents and income
sections.summary: According to an Institute of Policy Studies paper, one-third of riders have been in accidents requiring medical attention and the median income is less than $2,000.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The job can be dangerous, with one-third of riders having been in accidents that require medical attention, and the median income is less than $2,000, according to a paper by researchers at the Institute of Policy Studies (IPS).

sections.label: CPF Housing Grant increase
sections.summary: The Government will raise the CPF Housing Grant for first-time home buyer families purchasing resale HDB flats by $30,000 for 2-, 3- and 4-room flats and $10,000 for 5-room or larger flats, with first-time singles getting half the increase; analysts caution it may raise resale flat demand and prices.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The Government has announced that it will raise the CPF Housing Grant for first-time home buyer families purchasing resale HDB flats by $30,000 for those 2-, 3- and 4-room flats and by $10,000 for those buying 5-room or larger resale flats.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: First-time singles will get half the increase given to married couples.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: This increase in the CPF Housing Grant will be welcomed by many first-time home buyers, especially those who are looking to get a flat in a mature estate near their parents' home but have been unsuccessful in balloting for a BTO flat in a mature estate.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: However, some property analysts have cautioned that the increased grant amount may also raise demand and prices of resale flats.

sections.label: Government projections on flat prices
sections.summary: The passage states it is important to understand the Government's projections on how the CPF Housing Grant increase would elevate HDB flat prices over the next two years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: As such, it is important to understand the Government's projections on how this increase in the CPF Housing Grant would elevate HDB flat prices over the next two years.

sections.label: Housing grants for resale flats
sections.summary: It asks whether increasing housing grants will remain the Government's main approach to making resale flats affordable.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: More fundamentally, is increasing housing grants going to continue to be the Government's main approach to making resale flats affordable?

sections.label: Global trade growth projection
sections.summary: Global trade, a key driver of Singapore's GDP, is projected to grow slower than global GDP over the medium term.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: For the first time in a long, long time, global trade, a key driver of Singapore's GDP, is projected to grow slower than global GDP over the medium term.

sections.label: Budget 2022 revenue risk
sections.summary: Without the 2022 Budget moves, revenue risked not covering projected public expenditure, which has grown fast and will keep growing.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Without the Budget moves of 2022, we would have been at risk of not having enough revenue to cover projected public expenditure, which has grown fast in recent years and will continue to grow rapidly on the back of higher healthcare, social and infrastructure spending, let alone to deal with unexpected contingencies.

sections.label: Social spending growth
sections.summary: Social spending almost doubled between 2010 and 2019.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Social spending almost doubled between 2010 and 2019.

sections.label: Stronger support for three groups
sections.summary: It highlights three groups needing more specific support: middle-income Singaporeans who lose jobs, ex-offenders, and Singaporeans in debt.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: But while I recognise the efficiency and effectiveness of these broad-based measures, I also think we need to recognise that there are Singaporeans who are being pushed to their limits of adversity more than others and to be truly inclusive, we need to face up to this and push ourselves to consider whether it warrants more specific support for them to build resiliency.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: I will highlight three groups of residents today for whom I believe we might need a stronger trampoline: first, Singaporeans, in particular, middle-income Singaporeans, who lose their jobs; two, ex-offenders; and three, Singaporeans in debt.

sections.label: Redundancy or unemployment insurance proposal
sections.summary: MPs from both sides raised the possibility of implementing some form of redundancy or unemployment insurance amid retrenchment concerns.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: MPs from both sides of the House, including various Members of the Workers' Party and Mr Patrick Tay from the People's Action Party (PAP), have raised the possibility that with the increasingly volatile environment and whispers of more retrenchments, the time may have come for Singapore to implement some form of redundancy or unemployment insurance.

sections.label: Tiering ComCare assistance
sections.summary: ComCare could be tweaked to tier assistance by pre-job loss income, time-limited and subject to job search or reskilling.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: For example, we could tweak the ComCare scheme to tier the assistance level based on pre-job loss income – time-limited and subject to efforts to look for new jobs or attend suitable reskilling programmes.

sections.label: Supporting ex-offenders employment
sections.summary: Yellow Ribbon Singapore, employers and community support help ex-offenders, and the new Uplifting Employment Credit in Budget 2023 helps them find jobs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The efforts of organisations like Yellow Ribbon Singapore and the support of employers and the community in the form of counselling, resilience training, job flexibility and other forms of support have been instrumental in supporting ex-offenders on the ground.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: I am very glad to hear of the new Uplifting Employment Credit in Budget 2023 to help ex-offenders to find jobs.

sections.label: Couple ineligible for housing grant
sections.summary: A couple succeeded in their flat application but were not eligible for the Enhanced CPF Housing Grant because he had not worked 12 months before applying.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: He and his wife applied for a flat of their own.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: They were overjoyed to be successful in their application, only to learn that they were not eligible for the Enhanced CPF Housing Grant, because he had not worked for 12 months prior to the date of application for the flat.

sections.label: MSF on funding debt payment
sections.summary: MSF's view is that funding debt payment out of public resources is not appropriate given debts arise from personal decisions.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The Ministry of Social and Family Development’s (MSF) view has been that it is not appropriate to fund debt payment out of public resources given they arise out of personal decisions.

sections.label: Financial capability survey findings
sections.summary: The 2021 MoneySense survey found four in 10 respondents did not understand financial concepts and over half lacked retirement plans, prompting a call to strengthen financial capability programmes.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: While we have made progress in the 2021 MoneySense Financial Capability Survey, four in 10 respondents still did not understand financial concepts such as "simple and compound interest" and "risk diversification".

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: More than half of the respondents had not developed a plan for retirement savings.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: As financial resilience is a critical part of building personal resilience, I urge the Government to further strengthen the national financial capability programme such as by targeting specific segments with lower financial capabilities and in tandem with a stronger consumer protection framework.

sections.label: Youth and online pornography conversations
sections.summary: Few youth discussed the birds and the bees or online pornography with parents, and with high internet penetration youth spend much time on social media, harming well-being.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth and Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: In a dialogue I had with youth in their early to mid-20s some months ago, I asked the crowd I was in front of, "Growing up, how many of you had a conversation on the birds and the bees with your parents?" Of over 50 participants, a few raised their hands.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth and Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: I followed up by asking whether any of them had a conversation with their parents about dealing with online pornography, all of them stared blankly at each other.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth and Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: Internet penetration in Singapore first crossed the 50% mark in the year 2003.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth and Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: And today, it stands at more than 90%.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth and Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: The Internet – along with its many boons and banes – is here to stay.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth and Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: In an unprecedented fashion, our young ones spend much of their time and effort curating and manicuring their social media presence and in some cases, disproportionately and quite recklessly, I would say, vesting their self-worth in their online personas.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth and Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: Incessantly scrolling their way to poorer well-being, our youth are fighting an invisible but ongoing guerrilla war.

sections.label: Budget 2023 family boost
sections.summary: Budget 2023 offers a boost for Singaporean families.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth and Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: (In Mandarin):   Mdm Deputy Speaker, Budget 2023 offers a boost for Singaporean families.

sections.label: Singapore electricity consumption and gas
sections.summary: Singapore consumed over 53 terawatt-hours of electricity in 2021, with production 95% dependent on natural gas.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: As a nation, we consumed more than 53 terawatt-hours of electricity in 2021.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Currently, our electricity production is 95% dependent on natural gas, with two-thirds from Piped Natural Gas (PNG) and one-third from Liquefied Natural Gas (LNG).

sections.label: Hydrogen-ready power plant Jurong Island
sections.summary: Singapore's first hydrogen-ready power plant, hoping to supply 600 megawatts, will be built on Jurong Island, following the National Hydrogen Strategy launch.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Singapore's first hydrogen-ready power plant that hopes to supply 600 megawatts of energy will be built on Jurong Island.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: In October 2022, Deputy Prime Minister Wong launched the National Hydrogen Strategy to accelerate transition to net zero emissions and to strengthen energy security.

sections.label: Funding for sea level protection
sections.summary: Prime Minister Lee committed $100 billion or more in 2019, and $5 billion will be injected into the Coastal and Flood Protection Fund.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: During the National Day Rally in 2019, Prime Minister Lee committed $100 billion or more, to protect Singapore against rising sea levels.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: And in his recent Budget speech, Deputy Prime Minister Wong shared that $5 billion will be injected into the Coastal and Flood Protection Fund to support the construction of coastal and drainage infrastructure.

sections.label: Budget 2023 active aging employment
sections.summary: Budget 2023 encourages active aging through employment, with extension of Senior Employment Credit and Part-time Re-employment Grant until 2025.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: (In Malay):   Budget 2023 encourages active aging through employment.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: I strongly support the extension of the Senior Employment Credit and the Part-time Re-employment Grant until 2025 to support employers who offer part-time re-employment to eligible senior workers.

sections.label: Adjustments and employment insurance support
sections.summary: Workers must adjust job scopes and hours, and the insurance industry is urged to provide employment insurance beyond statutory age limits.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: They must be prepared to adjust their job scopes, lighten their responsibilities and shorten work hours.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: I also urge the insurance industry to support this initiative by providing employment insurance beyond statutory employment age limits.

sections.label: Baby bonus and paternity leave
sections.summary: The baby bonus and incentives are further enhanced and paternity leave is increased by 100%.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
sentences.text: The baby bonus as well as incentives are just further enhanced and paternal leave is increased by 100%.

sections.label: US nuclear fusion experiment
sections.summary: On 5 December, US scientists at the National Ignition Facility in California generated more energy from a nuclear fusion reaction than they put in.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
sentences.text: On 5 December last year, US scientists at the National Ignition Facility in California generated more energy from a nuclear fusion reaction than they put in.

sections.label: Energy 2050 Committee pathways
sections.summary: The Energy 2050 Committee identified three pathways for Singapore to achieve net-zero by 2050, one including nuclear energy.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
sentences.text: The Energy 2050 Committee has identified three pathways that Singapore could take to achieve net-zero by 2050, one of which includes the use of nuclear energy.

sections.label: Imported natural gas for electricity
sections.summary: Singapore currently relies on imported natural gas to generate around 95% of its electricity.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
sentences.text: Currently, we are relying on imported natural gas to generate around 95% of our electricity.

sections.label: Company wind-ups in 2022
sections.summary: In 2022, 205 companies were wound up, more than the 119 in 2021 and 201 in 2020.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
sentences.text: In 2022, last year, 205 companies were wound up, a higher number than in 2021 and 2020 when 119 and 201 companies respectively were shut for good.

sections.label: Challenges facing companies and SMEs
sections.summary: Companies face new challenges and rising costs, and SMEs accounting for over half of local employment must innovate and digitalise to thrive.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
sentences.text: Today, companies are confronted with a lot of new challenges, from workers preferring to work from home and interactions with colleagues and clients through e-meeting platforms, to the rise of e-commerce and e-banking.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
sentences.text: They are faced with huge rising costs in doing business, such as higher interest rates on their loans, higher rentals, a very tight labour market, higher wages due to our Progressive Wage Model (PWM) as well, a higher CPF ceiling coming up and more leaves for their workers because of childcare and paternity leave.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
sentences.text: Companies, particularly our small- and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs), that account for more than half of our local employment, can only continue to thrive if they can innovate, increase productivity through continual digital transformation and reduce their reliance on intensive manpower.

sections.label: Coastal defence project
sections.summary: The Prime Minister revealed a project costing $100 billion or more to build ponders and sea walls to protect low-lying areas and create new land.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
sentences.text: During the 2019 National Day Rally, Prime Minister revealed an ambitious $100 billion or more project to build ponders and sea walls not only to protect our low-lying areas from rising sea levels but also to create new land with exciting possibilities.

sections.label: Construction delays and flat queues
sections.summary: Delays and slowdowns in construction led to long queues for BTO flats and a frothy HDB resale market as people compete for limited supply.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Today, the lingering tail continues to be felt with the delays and slowdowns in construction culminating in long queues for Build-To-Order (BTO) flats and a frothy HDB resale market as people compete for the more limited supply of available flats.

sections.label: Interest rates and loan payments
sections.summary: MAS does not raise interest rates, but banks follow international benchmarks, so Singapore rates spiked, causing higher loan payments for borrowers including mortgages and trade loans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: In Singapore, the Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) does not raise interest rates, but the banks generally take the lead from international benchmarks when setting their own lending rates.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: So, this has meant that interest rates in Singapore have also spiked, causing higher loan payments for borrowers, which include the many mortgages as well as companies for their trade loans.

sections.label: Assistance for young couples
sections.summary: Young couples get more chances at BTO flats, more financial assistance for the resale market, and various support payments that would more than offset the rise in cost of living.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Young couples will now have more chances to get a BTO flat, there will be more financial assistance to tap into the resale market and there is a wide range of financial and social assistance being given out, including GST Vouchers, Cost of Living support payments, U-Save rebates and support for parents with children, all the way from babies to tertiary education and for lower-income groups, many of these measures would more than offset the rise in cost of living.

sections.label: Budget help for young families
sections.summary: This Budget assists young families with a second ballot for BTOs, higher resale flat grants, and children's expenses from birth through tertiary education.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Young families have also given feedback that difficulty getting flats and the rising cost of living have been deterring them from starting families.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: This Budget has comprehensive assistance for such young families – assistance in getting BTOs with a second ballot, higher grants to assist them to buy resale flats as an alternative and, importantly, assistance for children's expenses all the way from birth (Baby Bonus); preschool (CDA account top-up); school (Edusave top-up) and tertiary (PSEA top-up).

sections.label: Level playing field and income gaps
sections.summary: More can be done to promote equality of opportunity and social mobility, but a more level playing field alone does not justify vast and ever-increasing gaps in income, economic security and social respect.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: At the same time, I am sure we all recognise that more can be done to promote equality of opportunity and social mobility but beyond that, I want to put across another idea here today – that ensuring a more level playing field alone does not justify vast and ever-increasing gaps in income, economic security and social respect between those who do well in the academic and job arenas and those who do not.

sections.label: OPPI survey on meritocracy beliefs
sections.summary: An OPPI survey found Singaporeans believe in meritocracy, but those aged 18 to 25 have lower belief that Singapore society is equal and fair than older groups.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Interestingly, a survey by OPPI showed that whilst Singaporeans overwhelmingly believe in meritocracy, Singaporeans in the younger age group, 18 to 25 especially, have a lower belief that Singapore society is equal and fair compared to older age groups.

sections.label: Life expectancy education gap
sections.summary: A 2021 reply to a Parliamentary Question revealed a life expectancy gap of almost six years between those with post-secondary education and those without.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: After all, in reply to my Parliamentary Question in 2021, it was revealed that there was a gap in life expectancy in Singapore of almost six years between those with post-secondary education and those without.

sections.label: Meritocracy for equality and mobility
sections.summary: The passage calls for a meritocracy seeking equality of opportunity and social mobility, and also sustainability, a decent standard of living and societal respect.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Rather what we should seek is a meritocracy that strives for equality of opportunity and social mobility but going beyond that, one that ensures sustainability, a decent standard of living and societal respect, a levelling up for those who are less successful in conventional terms.

sections.label: Age of prime mover drivers
sections.summary: A CNA article reported some in the haulage industry estimate prime mover drivers' average age at 55, with younger drivers at 5% to 10% or less.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: According to a recent Channel NewsAsia (CNA) article on this topic, some in the haulage industry, for example, estimate the average age of prime mover drivers to be 55, with younger drivers accounting for 5% to 10% of the workforce or less.

sections.label: Budget 2023 National Productivity Fund top-up
sections.summary: In Budget 2023, the Government is making a $4 billion top-up to the National Productivity Fund.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In Budget 2023, the Government is making a $4 billion top-up to the National Productivity Fund (NPF).

sections.label: KPMG report on productivity scheme
sections.summary: A 2015 KPMG report said take-up rates rose but the scheme's productivity impact was muted, and value-added per worker fell in the latest quarter.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: A KPMG report from 2015 stated, "While take-up rates have gone up, the scheme's impact on productivity has been muted." Sir, our value-added per worker fell in the latest quarter, which underlines the challenge we are facing with productivity.

sections.label: Consultancy interest and productivity
sections.summary: Speaker declares consultancy chairmanship and asks if Government will take total factor productivity performance seriously.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: At this point, I declare my interest as the chairman of a research consultancy that undertakes economic and business consulting.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Also, will the Government take seriously our abysmal performance on total factor productivity (TFP) – a subject I have raised in the House previously?

sections.label: Compulsory free preschool proposal
sections.summary: Speaker proposes compulsory, completely free preschool for lower incomes, citing UNESCO 2020 findings and Singapore's 90% enrolment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: My suggestion is that the Government makes preschool education compulsory and completely free for those of lower incomes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: A UNESCO study conducted in 2020 found that 63 countries have adopted legal provisions for free pre-primary education and 51 countries have adopted pre-primary education as a compulsory level in national legal frameworks.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I know from a reply to my PQ last year that 90% of children in Singapore aged three to four are enrolled in preschool, but this proposal would make a difference to the 10%.

sections.label: SkillsFuture education loan proposal
sections.summary: Speaker asks if Government will consider a SkillsFuture education loan for adults unable to secure scholarships or retraining places.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Thirdly, would the Government consider a proposal for a SkillsFuture education loan to help fund Continuing Education and Training (CET) for adults who cannot competitively secure places among scholarships and places in retraining programmes like Professional Conversion Programmes (PCPs), a supply of which is still limited?

sections.label: Meritocracy backlash and justice
sections.summary: Speaker argues unbridled meritocracy causes backlash over distributive and contributive justice, citing US voting patterns and Oren Cass.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: An unbridled and heartless meritocracy inevitably leads to a backlash on those who feel disadvantaged and discriminated against because society undervalues and underpays for their skills, aptitudes and potential.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: It would be a backlash not only around distributive justice – the distribution of economic fruits – but also contributive justice – the right of citizens to contribute equally to society and to obtain dignity and recognition in making that contribution.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In the US, voting patterns have come to diverge between those with and without college degrees, with many non-college graduates turning to the kind of anti-systemic politics seen in the Capitol riot on 6 January 2021.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: As the writer Oren Cass said when speaking of the dangers of irresponsible populism, "The question is not whether the open agenda and a very laissez-faire unbridled meritocracy, will lose, but to what?" An extreme form of meritocracy and laissez-faire policies that elevate it, to some extent, unfairly, define as having merit too high and too harshly above all other people, cannot be sustained, as is the case with all tyrannies in the end.

sections.label: Workforce burnout mental health
sections.summary: Speaker states 57% of the workforce said burnout was the leading factor affecting their mental health during the pandemic.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
sentences.text: On our shores, our workforce is burnt out – 57% of our workforce said burnout was the leading factor affecting their mental health during the pandemic.

sections.label: Youth mental health symptoms study
sections.summary: Speaker cites a study of over 3,000 young people finding one in three Singapore youths reported internalising mental health symptoms.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
sentences.text: In the Singapore Youth Epidemiology and Resilience Study last year involving over 3,000 young people aged 11 to 18, it was found that one in three youths in Singapore has reported internalising mental health symptoms.

sections.label: Growth model and ageing workforce
sections.summary: Economic growth and rising productivity demands amid an ageing workforce and possible zero labour force growth are taking a toll, prompting a call to consider a different model of progress.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
sentences.text: Economic growth and the ever-growing demand for increased productivity despite a rapidly ageing workforce and potentially zero growth in our labour force is taking a toll on a whole generation of people.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
sentences.text: I urge this House and Singaporeans to seriously consider a different model of progress.

sections.label: Coal depletion by 2090
sections.summary: According to the Millennium Alliance for Humanity and the biosphere at Stanford University, the world will be out of coal by 2090.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
sentences.text: The stark reality: according to the Millennium Alliance for Humanity and the biosphere at Stanford University, the world will be out of coal by 2090.

sections.label: Oil depletion in 47 years
sections.summary: The Statistical Review of World Energy through British Petroleum and other sources indicates that at current consumption rates, oil will run out in 47 years.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
sentences.text: In the Statistical Review of World Energy through British Petroleum as well as many other sources, it tells us that at our current rate of consumption, we will be out of oil in 47 years’ time.

sections.label: Youth climate change anxiety survey
sections.summary: In a survey of 10,000 youths including Singaporean youth, close to 60% were very or extremely worried about climate change, with 45% saying the anxiety negatively affects daily life.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
sentences.text: In a survey of 10,000 youths, including Singaporean youth, close to 60% have felt “very” or “extremely” worried about climate change, with 45% reporting that this anxiety negatively affects their daily lives.

sections.label: Share More Use Less motto
sections.summary: The motto is "Share More, Use Less, Waste Not".

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
sentences.text: The motto is "Share More, Use Less, Waste Not".

sections.label: Nee Soon South Shwap initiative
sections.summary: A sharing culture has begun in Nee Soon South with a piloted "Shwap" initiative for pre-loved clothing, which is intended to be extended to other daily use items for neighbourhood swapping.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
sentences.text: Creating a sharing culture has already begun in Nee Soon South, where we piloted a “Shwap” initiative for people to “shop” for pre-loved clothing that others would like to give away.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
sentences.text: I intend to extend this effort beyond clothing to other daily use items, so that within our neighbourhoods, people can swap items they no longer need for items that others want to give away.

sections.label: Nature-based pedagogy in early education
sections.summary: The speaker urges extending nature-based pedagogy to early childhood and primary education so children become "Nature Natives".

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
sentences.text: This needs to start as early in life as possible, so that our current children can be “Nature Natives” and not just “Digital Natives” in the new global reality.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
sentences.text: I urge that we make it a top priority and extend nature-based pedagogy to our early childhood and primary education.

sections.label: Forward Singapore social and ecological well-being
sections.summary: Forward Singapore should rally citizens towards a future where social and ecological well-being is valued equally with economic well-being.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
sentences.text: Forward Singapore should be an exercise ambitious and daring enough to rally our citizenry towards the big picture – a future where Social and Ecological well-being is valued equally with economic well-being.

sections.label: Coordinating Ministry for Wellness proposal
sections.summary: The speaker urges setting up a Coordinating Ministry for Wellness so Ministries work together to ensure the wellness of people and planet.
