sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
sentences.text: To do this, Ministries including National Development, Sustainability and Environment, Health, Manpower, Trade and Industry must work together and adopt a lens of ensuring the wellness of our people and planet is adopted across all efforts.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
sentences.text: I urge the Government to set up a Coordinating Ministry for Wellness help implement this, to land a sustainability land across all Ministries.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
sentences.text: Imagine a society that consumes less, with people who work less but connects more and are happier and healthier for it.

sections.label: Deputy Prime Minister Wong support measures
sections.summary: Deputy Prime Minister Wong introduced support measures including the Enterprise Financing Scheme, Energy Efficiency Grant, GST Voucher scheme and Assurance Package.

sentences.speaker: Prof Koh Lian Pin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Deputy Prime Minister Wong also introduced several support measures, including the Enterprise Financing Scheme, the Energy Efficiency Grant, the permanent GST Voucher scheme and the Assurance Package to support our businesses, our workers and our families.

sections.label: Carbon tax and carbon credits
sections.summary: The revised carbon tax policy will let carbon-tax liable companies offset up to 5% of taxable emissions with high-quality carbon credits.

sentences.speaker: Prof Koh Lian Pin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: For example, our revised carbon tax policy will soon allow carbon-tax liable companies to use high-quality carbon credits to offset up to 5% of their taxable carbon emissions.

sentences.speaker: Prof Koh Lian Pin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The global voluntary carbon credit market was worth about US$2 billion dollars in 2021 and is expected to grow in value to between US$10 billion and US$40 billion in 2030.

sections.label: Carbon credits and accounting R&D
sections.summary: Carbon credits shift capital across sectors and borders for nature-based solutions, so investing in credible carbon accounting R&D is vital.

sentences.speaker: Prof Koh Lian Pin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Carbon credits and carbon markets in general, are ways of shifting capital across sectors and across borders to help us implement these nature-based solutions at scale.

sentences.speaker: Prof Koh Lian Pin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: However, to ensure genuine climate and societal benefits, it is vital to invest in the R&D of credible carbon accounting and monitoring methodologies.

sections.label: Carbon Integrity SG research programme
sections.summary: NUS launched Carbon Integrity SG with National Research Foundation support to develop carbon accounting methodologies for Southeast Asia's ecosystems.

sentences.speaker: Prof Koh Lian Pin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: For example, with support from the National Research Foundation, the National University of Singapore (NUS) recently launched a new research programme called Carbon Integrity SG.

sentences.speaker: Prof Koh Lian Pin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Carbon Integrity SG will enable Singapore researchers to work with regional universities, Government agencies, businesses and civil society to develop more robust and more accurate carbon accounting methodologies for Southeast Asia's ecosystems, to ensure the supply of high-quality forest carbon credits to meet our needs and market demands.

sections.label: Decarbonisation as top priority
sections.summary: Avoiding or reducing carbon emissions sits at the top of the climate mitigation hierarchy, so decarbonisation must remain Singapore's top priority.

sentences.speaker: Prof Koh Lian Pin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Avoiding or reducing carbon emissions sits at the top rung of our climate mitigation hierarchy.

sentences.speaker: Prof Koh Lian Pin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In other words, decarbonisation must remain our top priority as Singapore transitions towards a low-carbon society.

sections.label: Rare disease numbers in Singapore
sections.summary: About 2,500 people are estimated to have a rare disease in Singapore, and about 7,500 people including immediate family members are directly impacted.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: About 2,500 people are estimated to have a rare disease in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: When we include their immediate family members, we are looking at approximately 7,500 people directly impacted by rare disorders.

sections.label: Rare disease medicine costs
sections.summary: Minister for Health Ong Ye Kung stated last November that medicines for rare disease patients can exceed $200,000 per patient annually.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: As Minister for Health Ong Ye Kung stated last November, medicines for rare disease patients can exceed $200,000 per patient annually.

sections.label: Respite care for severe disabilities
sections.summary: A speaker appeals to the team reviewing hubs' service offerings to consider needs of people with severe disabilities who are not work-capable and expand respite care.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: On behalf of the caregivers of people with disabilities, I would like to sincerely appeal to the team looking into the service offerings of the hubs, to consider the needs of people with severe disabilities who are not work-capable, and so, expand the provision of respite care that is much needed for the caregivers of this group.

sections.label: Inclusive workplaces for caregivers
sections.summary: The passage asks whether schemes can make workplaces more inclusive towards caregivers of persons with severe disabilities, encouraging companies to redesign work for flexibility.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: Just as we have schemes to encourage companies to hire seniors and PwDs, may we consider putting in place schemes to make our workplaces more inclusive towards caregivers of persons with these severe disabilities?

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: Can we look at how to encourage more companies to consider redesigning their work across job roles, allowing for greater flexibility for those that require it, not as a lifestyle preference, but out of necessity and livelihood?

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: We can, and must do more for this group of Singaporeans, to strengthen our social compact to build a Singapore Made for Families as Budget 2023 articulates, in all its diversity.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: Let us remember and support these caregivers and family members of people with severe disabilities, with their employment efforts for sustainable living.

sections.label: Working Mother's Child Relief concerns
sections.summary: Members raised concerns over the Working Mother's Child Relief, which has been adjusted.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Over many speeches during this debate, Members have raised concerns over the Working Mother's Child Relief, which has been adjusted.

sections.label: Foreign parental leave systems
sections.summary: The passage lists maternity, health, hospital, baby box and paternity leave systems in the UK, France, Germany, Finland and Iceland.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: The UK has a 52-week maternity leave system, perhaps to be introduced with Swedish flexibility, to take up the leave up to the age of eight for the child.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: French maternity health coverage from prenatal to post delivery, German hospital coverage for up to 12 days after birth, Finland's "baby box" system upon childbirth and aspire towards Iceland's 90% take-up rate for paternity leave.

sections.label: Banning sales to next cohort
sections.summary: The speaker favours a generational break banning sales to the next cohort of youths, as adopted by New Zealand.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: But I see less sense in increasing taxes for a product with inelastic demand and users that are less likely to change their behaviour.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Therefore, we should take a bolder move to undertake a generational break and ban sales to the next cohort of youths, such as adopted by New Zealand.

sections.label: Help for those affected
sections.summary: The passage asks what can be done to help those truly affected by the increase and whether there will be a future review.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: True, we could encourage them to sell and monetise, but often, these decisions are not just economic ones, they are emotive ones as well: they have raised a family here, they have grown up here, they have lived here all their lives.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: So, what can we do to help those who are truly affected by the increase?

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Will there be a review of this in the future?

sections.label: Singaporeans standing united
sections.summary: The passage states Singaporeans must not be underestimated in standing united, as the Budget theme re-emphasises.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: We must not underestimate Singaporeans and our ability to stand united as one, especially in the face of crisis and challenges.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: This year's Budget themed as "Charting Our New Way Forward Together" re-emphasises that.

sections.label: 2023 Budget expansionary
sections.summary: The passage states the 2023 Budget is expansionary, not contractionary, contrary to Assoc Prof Jamus Lim.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: At the macro level, the 2023 Budget is expansionary, not contractionary – contrary to what Assoc Prof Jamus Lim said yesterday.

sections.label: COVID-19 spending and Past Reserves
sections.summary: The Government spent $72 billion fighting COVID-19, with $40 billion drawn from Past Reserves.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: The Government had spent $72 billion to fight COVID-19, of which $40 billion came from Past Reserves.

sections.label: Government spending as share of GDP
sections.summary: Government spending is expected to rise from 18% of GDP to 20% by 2030, with ageing and healthcare costs cited.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: On the expenditure side, we expect Government spending that is now at 18% of GDP to reach 20% by 2030.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: But here, I should emphasise that it is important to look at these fiscal projections as a percentage of GDP and not in nominal dollar terms, which Mr Leong had done.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: And he had suggested that we had somehow been imprudent in our spending, because our spending now exceeds $100 billion compared to pre-COVID-19 levels of about $85 billion. "What a large increase", he says.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: In fact, between FY2019 and now, our spending remains at about the same proportion of GDP, which is around 18%.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: But looking ahead, with an ageing population and rising healthcare costs, we expect this to rise to around 20% of GDP by FY2030.

sections.label: GST increase and fiscal position
sections.summary: The tight fiscal position requires proceeding with the second GST increase in 2024 as planned.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: But the bottom line is that our tight fiscal position is very much a reality over the medium term.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: That is why we have to proceed with the second step of the increase in GST in 2024 as planned.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Deferring this will only store up more problems for the future and will leave us with less resources to take care of our growing number of seniors.

sections.label: GST delay for households
sections.summary: The AP is intended to delay the GST impact by five years for most Singaporean households and 10 years for lower-income households.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: The AP is intended to delay the impact of the GST by five years for the majority of Singaporean households and by 10 years for the lower-income households.

sections.label: Singapore tax-to-GDP ratio
sections.summary: After Budgets 2022 and 2023 including the full GST increase, Singapore's tax-to-GDP ratio is 14%.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Besides having a diversified revenue base, we also pay attention to the overall tax burden.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: And after factoring the changes in Budgets 2022 and 2023, including the full GST increase, Singapore’s tax-to-GDP ratio is 14%.

sections.label: Taxes paid versus benefits received
sections.summary: For every dollar paid in taxes, one group received about $0.30 in benefits and another around $4.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: In recent years, for every dollar they paid in taxes, they received only about $0.30 in benefits.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: For every dollar they paid in taxes, they received around $4 in benefits.

sections.label: Median household real income growth
sections.summary: Median household real income per household member grew more than 3% per annum over the last decade.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Growth of median household real income per household member in Singapore over the last decade was more than 3% per annum.

sections.label: Middle quintile effective tax burden
sections.summary: The effective tax burden for middle quintile households is around 10% of income, including indirect taxes.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: I have shared earlier the low overall tax burden for Singapore, that was expressed as a percentage of GDP, as a percentage of our economy.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: But you can translate that to households and when you look at households in the middle quintile and the total taxes paid – total taxes, not just personal income tax but other indirect taxes as well – the effective tax burden is around 10% of income.

sections.label: Tax burden lower than other countries
sections.summary: Incomplete data show Singapore's tax burden is significantly lower than that of these countries.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Not all the data are complete, we got what we could.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: And they clearly show that our tax burden is significantly lower than that of these countries.

sections.label: Leong statement called falsehood
sections.summary: What Mr Leong said is an outright falsehood.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: What Mr Leong said is an outright falsehood.

sections.label: Middle 20% benefits versus taxes
sections.summary: For the middle 20%, benefits received were about twice the amount paid in taxes.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: In particular, for the middle 20%, the amount of benefits they received was about twice the amount they paid in taxes.

sections.label: Growing economic pie focus
sections.summary: Singapore remains focused on growing the economic pie so Singaporeans can build better lives.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Have we moved from a '"pro-growth" to a "pro-redistribution" approach?

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We remain focused on growing the economic pie, because only then can Singaporeans build better lives for themselves and their families.

sections.label: National Productivity Fund expansion
sections.summary: Additional resources are set aside and the National Productivity Fund's scope is expanded to anchor quality investments and be more competitive.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We must work hard to be more competitive and anchor more quality investments.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: And that is why we are setting aside additional resources and expanding the scope of the National Productivity Fund.

sections.label: SME capability building grants
sections.summary: Support to SMEs through capability building grants like the Productivity Solutions Grant, Enterprise Development Grant and Market Readiness Assistance Grant doubled between 2019 and 2022.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: In fact, the amount of support extended to SMEs through capability building grants, like the Productivity Solutions Grant, the Enterprise Development Grant and the Market Readiness Assistance Grant doubled between 2019 and 2022.

sections.label: Progressive Wage Credit Scheme support
sections.summary: This Budget includes measures for immediate cost pressures, with the Government taking on 75% of wage increase costs under the Progressive Wage Credit Scheme.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: And in this Budget, we have rolled out some measures to help businesses with some of their immediate cost pressures.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: This includes the Government taking on a major share, 75%, of the cost of wage increases under the Progressive Wage Credit Scheme.

sections.label: Green transition preparations
sections.summary: More must be done to prepare businesses, workers and the economy for the green transition, following last year's net-zero target and carbon tax trajectory announcements.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: There is clearly much more we will need to do to prepare businesses, workers and our economy for this green transition.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: I had announced several significant moves in last year's Budget, including our net-zero target and the carbon tax trajectory.

sections.label: GoBusiness portal access
sections.summary: SMEs can use the GoBusiness portal for cross-agency access to over 100 Government assistance schemes.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: For example, SMEs can tap on the GoBusiness portal which offers convenient cross-agency access to over 100 Government assistance schemes.

sections.label: Jobs-Skills Integrators
sections.summary: The Jobs-Skills Integrators is the next move to strengthen the training and placement ecosystem for workers.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: The Jobs-Skills Integrators is the next move to strengthen the training and placement ecosystem for our workers.

sections.label: Jobs-Skills Integrators pilot sectors
sections.summary: Singapore studied Sweden and Switzerland's formalised role and will pilot Jobs-Skills Integrators in three sectors with more SMEs and mature workers.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: But we have studied the experience of other countries, like Sweden and Switzerland, which have formalised such a role, and seen some positive outcomes.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: And that is why we decided to pilot the Jobs-Skills Integrators in three sectors for a start and we have chosen sectors where there are more SMEs and more mature workers.

sections.label: Support for displaced mature workers
sections.summary: Many take the first available job even if it is not a good fit, so support for displaced and mature workers is being studied.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Instead, many will just take the first job available, even if it is not such a good fit for them.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: That is why we are studying how we can better support our displaced and mature workers through these challenging transitions and setbacks.

sections.label: Targeted re-employment support consideration
sections.summary: Unemployment benefits elsewhere made staying unemployed attractive, so targeted re-employment support is being considered to strengthen the SkillsFuture ecosystem.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: This is, again, not theoretical because we have seen the results of unemployment benefits offered in other places where displaced workers receive generous benefits, but they then find it more attractive to stay unemployed than to get back into the workforce.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: So, what we really should be thinking about is more like targeted re-employment support.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Ultimately, we want to help Singaporeans bounce back stronger from any setback that they may encounter throughout their careers.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: So, we will consider this and other moves to strengthen our SkillsFuture ecosystem and we are, in fact, deliberating and looking at this very carefully because our workers will always be at the heart of our economic strategies.

sections.label: Social support for larger families
sections.summary: Packages give more help to larger families with young and elderly dependents, and social support schemes and means-testing criteria will be reviewed.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: That is why we have designed our packages to provide more help for larger families with young and elderly dependents.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: And we will continue to review our social support schemes and their means-testing criteria, taking onboard all your suggestions, including the Annual Value (AV) thresholds, to ensure that Singaporeans in need receive the support that they need.

sections.label: HDB resale prices fall
sections.summary: HDB resale prices fell for six consecutive years from 2013 to 2019, a period the speaker observed at MND.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: I say this with some perspective because I was in the Ministry of National Development (MND) during the period when HDB resale prices came tumbling down.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: They fell for six consecutive years from 2013 to 2019.

sections.label: Constitutional safeguards for CV post
sections.summary: The CV post is safeguarded in the Constitution, with appointment and removal subject to the President's veto, so the Government does not influence the CV's decision.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: In fact, it is precisely because we do not want the Government to influence the CV's decision that we have safeguarded the post of the CV in the Constitution and made the appointment and removal of the post subject to the President's veto.

sections.label: Reserve price for tenders
sections.summary: A reserve price is set at 85% of an estimated market value determined by the CV.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We set a reserve price for these tenders.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: It is at 85% of an estimated market value as determined by the CV.

sections.label: Land pricing and flat prices
sections.summary: The way land is priced cannot simply be changed to bring down the selling price of flats.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: The bottom line is you cannot just change the way land is priced to bring down the selling price of flats.

sections.label: Priority for families and couples
sections.summary: Greater priority and an additional ballot go to families with children and married couples aged 40 and below buying their first home, and the CPF Housing Grant for resale flats is increased.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: In particular, we are giving greater priority to families with children and married couples aged 40 and below, who are buying their first home, and the additional ballot will significantly increase their chances of securing a BTO flat, especially one in a non-mature estate.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: And we are increasing the CPF Housing Grant for resale flats, so that eligible first-timer families and singles with more urgent needs can purchase a resale flat.

sections.label: Resale buyers receiving CPF grant
sections.summary: Based on resale transaction data over the last two years, only about one-third of resale flat buyers received the CPF Housing Grant.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Based on the data on resale transactions over the last two years, only about one-third of resale flat buyers received the CPF Housing Grant.

sections.label: Food service workers coming on board
sections.summary: Next month, workers in food services, as well as administrators and drivers, will come on board.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Next month, workers in food services, as well as administrators and drivers will come on board.

sections.label: ITE graduates employment outcomes
sections.summary: Through programmes like the Work-Study and Technical Diplomas, ITE graduates are seeing better employment outcomes, with median starting salaries comparable to those of polytechnic diploma graduates.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: In fact, through programmes like the Work-Study and Technical Diplomas, ITE graduates are seeing better employment outcomes, with median starting salaries that are comparable to those of polytechnic diploma graduates.

sections.label: Family-centric ComLink support
sections.summary: Common functions like outreach, befriending and case support are streamlined under ComLink to serve 14,000 families with children in rental housing.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: But in the end, our approach cannot be scheme-centric; it must be family-centric.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: That is why we are streamlining common functions such as outreach, befriending and case support under ComLink to serve the 14,000 families with children living in rental housing.

sections.label: Support for seniors
sections.summary: Seniors receive benefits under the enhanced Assurance Package and GST Voucher scheme, and retirement and re-employment ages are raised with employment support.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: For example, seniors will receive significant benefits under the enhanced Assurance Package and the GST Voucher scheme.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: I also agree with Members that those who wish to continue working should be well supported to do so.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: That is why the Government is progressively raising the retirement and re-employment ages and providing substantial employment support for seniors.

sections.label: CPF monthly salary ceiling
sections.summary: The CPF monthly salary ceiling is progressively raised to keep pace with the 80th percentile of monthly resident wages and help middle-income Singaporeans save more.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: That is why we have been working hard to boost the retirement adequacy of different cohorts and segments.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: It is the reason why we are progressively raising the CPF monthly salary ceiling.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: The increase is intended to keep pace with the 80th percentile of monthly resident wages, which crossed $8,000 last year, and to help middle-income Singaporeans save more for retirement.

sections.label: Phasing in CPF increase
sections.summary: The increase is phased in over four years after consulting tripartite partners, engaging them and listening to their concerns.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Importantly, they will be able to save more and strengthen their retirement security in the longer term.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We are phasing in this increase over four years because we have consulted our tripartite partners, engaged them and listened to their concerns.

sections.label: Enhanced Home Caregiving Grant
sections.summary: The enhancement of the Home Caregiving Grant was announced earlier and the enhanced grant takes effect next month.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Indeed, we had earlier announced the enhancement of the Home Caregiving Grant, and the enhanced grant will take effect next month.

sections.label: NIRC share of Budget
sections.summary: Out of every dollar spent in the Budget, 20 cents come from the NIRC.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Out of every dollar we spend in our Budget, 20 cents come from the NIRC.

sections.label: 2009 Past Reserves draw debate
sections.summary: In 2009 Parliament debated drawing $4.9 billion of Past Reserves to help Singaporeans through the Global Financial Crisis, and Mr Low Thia Khiang expressed surprise at the need.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Because in 2009, when this Parliament debated whether to draw $4.9 billion of Past Reserves that year to help Singaporeans tide over the Global Financial Crisis, Mr Low Thia Khiang then from the Workers' Party expressed surprise at the need to do so.

sections.label: Unlikely to restore $40 billion
sections.summary: The speaker said in the Budget Statement that it is highly unlikely the $40 billion drawn from Past Reserves will be put back.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Many things were not right, but that one thing was done right.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: This time, I explained in the Budget Statement that we are highly unlikely to put back the $40 billion drawn from Past Reserves.

sections.label: Calls to spend more reserves
sections.summary: The repeated calls were for the Government to spend more from the reserves, slow reserve growth, increase the 50% NIRC formula and change the reserves rules.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Instead, their repeated calls have been for the Government to spend more from the reserves – to slow down the growth of the reserves, increase the 50% NIRC formula, change the reserves rules.

sections.label: GST increase and redistribution
sections.summary: The speaker agrees fiscal redistribution should not pit groups against each other, welcomes Workers' Party support for the Budget including the GST increase, and says those who earn more should pay more.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: I also agree with Mr Pritam Singh's remarks that fiscal redistribution should not be about pitting one group against another.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: And I am very glad that the Workers' Party supports the Budget this year even though it includes the second step of the GST rate increase.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: The Workers' Party shares the Government's view that those who earn more should pay more in taxes, yet it consistently refuses to acknowledge the unique way the People's Action Party Government has implemented our GST system, which requires the well off to contribute more and does not hurt the poor.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We have to do what is right for Singapore and Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: And when tough calls like raising the GST have to be made, we have to be upfront, explain our position and persuade Singaporeans why such painful decisions are necessary but will ultimately benefit everyone.

sections.label: Moving forward as one people
sections.summary: The speaker says Singaporeans rally together, will not mortgage the future of the next generation, and had 55 speakers over the last three days.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We rally together through thick and thin and we move forward as one people.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We will never mortgage the future of our children in the next generation but we will do everything we can to give them a better start in their lifetimes.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: And they will enable us to secure our prospects and build a brighter future together – as one united people and as one Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
sentences.text: We have had 55 speakers over the last three days.

sections.label: 2018 CPI measurement request
sections.summary: In 2018, Mr Leon Perera asked the Government to consider measuring the consumer price index for specific demographic groups like young couples, parents with children and retirees.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: On this note, in 2018, my colleague Mr Leon Perera asked the Government to consider measuring the consumer price index (CPI), which tracks inflation for specific demographic groups like young couples, parents with children and retirees.

sections.label: Home Ownership Programme funding
sections.summary: More fiscal resources are being diverted to the Home Ownership Programme, from $1 billion in the past to $4 billion now.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Again that the fact of the matter is more and more money, more and more fiscal resources are being diverted to the Home Ownership Programme – $1 billion in the past, touching $4 billion now.

sections.label: BTO subsidies disclosure query
sections.summary: The Finance Minister did not clarify whether the Government will reveal subsidies for each Build-To-Order programme, which the speaker says shows inequity.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The Finance Minister did not, of course, clarify some of the specific queries that I raised in my speech about this insofar as whether the Government will reveal the subsidies for each Build-To-Order (BTO) programme because it shows that, actually, there is a point of inequity that I think needs to be worked on.

sections.label: Estimates Committee CFE KPIs
sections.summary: Paragraph 29 says the Estimates Committee expressed the need for robust KPI setting, monitoring and accountability of initiatives under CFE including ITMs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: But, of course, there are some domestic sectors where there are issues.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: And paragraph 29 says that the Committee, this being the Estimates Committee, expressed the need for robust KPI setting, monitoring and accountability of the various initiatives under CFE including ITMs.

sections.label: ITM allocation 2016
sections.summary: In the spirit of fiscal prudence, $4.5 billion was allocated to the ITMs in 2016.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: Because in the spirit of fiscal prudence, $4.5 billion dollars was allocated to the ITMs in 2016.

sections.label: Temasek in NIRC formula
sections.summary: Temasek was included in the NIRC formula because of more needs, healthcare needs and an ageing population.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: You have Temasek being included in the NIRC formula.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: Because we were told there were more needs, healthcare needs, ageing population.

sections.label: Managing spending needs and revenues
sections.summary: The government will manage growing spending needs while keeping finances stable, possibly raising revenues or re-allocating expenditure to new priority areas.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: In that light, we will continue to look at how we can manage growing spending needs, while keeping our finances stable and sustainable.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: There may be a need for additional revenues.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: And, if so, we will make sure that any form of additional revenues raised or taxes raised, are done in a way that keeps our overall system of taxes and benefits fair and progressive.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: We could also look at meeting increased spending needs, not only through increased revenues and taxes, but we could also do it through re-allocation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: So, there will also be a continual exercise to examine what are some areas that we can do less of, what are some things we might want to discontinue so that expenditure and funding can be re-allocated to new priority areas.

sections.label: Workers' Party reserves position shift
sections.summary: The speaker says Mr Singh acknowledged a change in the Workers' Party's position on putting back reserves, and disagrees with his comparison to Temasek's staged Net Investment Returns involvement.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Then, on the shift in the Workers' Party's position on the putting back of reserves, I am glad that Mr Singh has acknowledged that it is a change in the Workers' Party's position.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: But I would respectfully disagree with his comparing that with how we have updated our position on the involvement of Temasek in the Net Investment Returns framework.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Because we have made it very clear when we embarked on this that we did want Temasek to come in it.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: But it was a matter that needed more time to study and therefore, the implementation was staged.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: It is about fiscal prudence, discipline, responsibility, stewardship.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: That is consistent and has not changed and will not change, whereas, it seems to me, on that part, the Workers' Party has shifted.

sections.label: First paragraph observations, second call
sections.summary: The first paragraph contains observations and a question, not a call to action, which is in the second paragraph.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The first paragraph contains observations and poses a question that does not amount to a call to action.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The second paragraph is the call to action.

sections.label: Call to action on BTO
sections.summary: The observations were made in the questions posed, while the call to action is in the second paragraph saying BTO projects should continue.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: So, it is in that context that those observations were made in the questions posed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: But the call to action comes in the second paragraph which says BTO projects should continue.

sections.label: Demographia home price affordability bands
sections.summary: Demographia regards HPI above five as extremely or critically unaffordable, three to five as moderately unaffordable, and three and below as affordable.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera
sentences.text: Demographia regards anything above five for HPI as extremely or critically unaffordable; three to five as moderately unaffordable in some way; and three and below is affordable.

sections.label: Private vacancies and BTO supply
sections.summary: The write-up says private vacancies have only started to inch down with around 12,000 private units completing up to 2022, and asks whether HDB will have a vacancy rate problem compounded by 6,000 to 17,000 BTO units.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: The write-up says and I read, “that private vacancies in the private sector have only started to inch down but there are still around 12,000 private units completing up to 2022." So, with that, comparing now, HDB, "will the HDB have a vacancy rate problem compounded by a still steady stream of 6,000 to 17,000 BTO units in the last few years, which will continue to increase supply up to 2022.” The assessment was very clear.

sections.label: Affordability benchmarks and mortgage servicing ratio
sections.summary: Affordability benchmarks are not just home price to income ratio; the mortgage servicing ratio of 25% is also looked at.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: And our affordability benchmarks are not just expressed in home price to income ratio.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: We also look at the mortgage servicing ratio which is 25%.

sections.label: Contingency funds balance reduction
sections.summary: The Budget Statement proposed reducing contingency funds balance from $16 billion to $6 billion, after it rose from $3 billion to $16 billion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: The second question is in his Budget Statement speech, he talked about this contingency funds where we are going to reduce the balance from $16 billion to $6 billion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: It used to be from $3 billion to $16 billion; and then now we are going to $6 billion.

sections.label: Fiscal outlook transparency commitment
sections.summary: The government commits to updating information and being transparent about fiscal outlook, having raised funds to $16 billion during the pandemic.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: So, we are committed to updating, providing information as and when necessary, and being upfront and transparent about our fiscal outlook.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: We raised it to $16 billion during the pandemic because of the emergency situation we were facing.

sections.label: Constitutional amendment for contingency funds
sections.summary: Given new environment, the proposal is to reduce to $6 billion, requiring a constitutional amendment and a Bill tabled soon.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: But we thought given the new environment, the shocks and disruptions we may face, we could make it a bit bigger than what it used to be, but not at $16 billion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Hence, the proposal to come down to $6 billion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: But because we need a constitutional amendment to effect this, we will have to table a Bill in this House very soon.

sections.label: Investment returns on 1%
sections.summary: Investment returns on 1% cannot exceed the entire 1% unless reserves earn 200% per annum.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Mathematically speaking, there is no way the investment returns on that 1% can be higher revenue than the entire 1% itself, unless we are getting investment returns of 200% per annum from our reserves.

sections.label: CPF salary ceiling changes
sections.summary: The monthly CPF salary ceiling is changing to the 80th percentile, but there is no plan to update the annual ceiling.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: On the CPF salary ceiling, we are changing the monthly salary ceiling but there is no plan now to update the annual ceiling.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Because we think at the monthly level, there is a need to update to the 80th percentile.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: But at the annual level, the current ceiling still remains relevant.

sections.label: Removal of annual value tax
sections.summary: Removal of annual value tax on owner-occupied properties coincided with a more progressive property tax rate schedule, now a progressive wealth tax.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: So, the removal of this annual value tax on owner-occupied properties was done in the same time, as we really updated our property tax rate schedule to be much more progressive.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: And therefore, this is what we have now, not a separate tax on an annual value, but a property tax, which is a progressive wealth tax on everyone in Singapore.

sections.label: Package impact on inflation
sections.summary: The package targets lower-income groups and gives some to middle-incomes, with manageable inflation impact expected.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: We have targeted the lower-income groups, we have given some to the middle-incomes as well.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: But based on the design of the package, we believe that the impact on inflation will be manageable.

sections.label: IMF Article 4 figures
sections.summary: The IMF's July 2022 Article 4 projected a gross operating balance of positive 2.7% of GDP and net lending and borrowing at 1.4% of GDP.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: But I think we should not confuse an accounting approach with the actual net impact of the Government on the economy.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: So, to that effect, the IMF's Article 4, issued in July 2022, did state that the gross operating balance was projected to be positive 2.7% of GDP, and net lending and borrowing at 1.4% of GDP.

sections.label: Budget expansionary or contractionary assessment
sections.summary: Budgets are run through models to assess impact, with the assessment being slight expansionary support for the economy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: So, when we talk about whether a budget is expansionary or contractionary, we run it through our models, we assess what the impact will be.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: And as I said, our assessment is that, there will be a slight expansionary support for the economy.

sections.label: Redundancy insurance for displaced workers
sections.summary: Redundancy insurance or support for displaced workers is something that will continue to be studied.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: On the redundancy insurance or the support that we are thinking about for displaced workers, it is something we will continue to study.

sections.label: Empowering individuals on careers
sections.summary: Like Healthier SG empowering individuals on health, a similar approach is needed to engage and empower individuals to plan ahead for their careers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Very much as how we talk about Healthier SG as a movement where we can empower individuals to take charge of their own health.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: I think we need a similar way of reaching out, engaging and empowering individuals to start thinking and planning ahead for their own careers.

sections.label: BTO subsidies and land cost
sections.summary: A question asks whether the Deputy Prime Minister has factored in BTO subsidies and land cost in the equation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Can I ask whether the Deputy Prime Minister has factored in BTO subsidies and land cost in the equation?

sections.label: NIRC amount and spending percentage
sections.summary: Asks the Deputy Prime Minister how much NIRC has been tucked away in total to-date and what percentage is spent yearly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Can the Deputy Prime Minister share with us how much NIRC has been tucked away in total to-date and what percentage of that we spent every year?

sections.label: Nominal GDP and expenditure increase
sections.summary: Seeks confirmation that nominal GDP growth rose 33% from 2019 to 2023, matching expenditure rising from $75 billion to $100 billion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Can I confirm with the Deputy Prime Minister that nominal GDP growth had indeed increased by 33% from 2019 to 2023, which is exactly that increase in expenditure from 2019 to 2023, from $75 billion to $100, that is 33%.

sections.label: Assessment of reserves raid
sections.summary: States the assessment that this is clearly a raid on the reserves.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Our assessment is that this is clearly a raid on the reserves.

sections.label: CPF system parameters review
sections.summary: States the starting point is to look at the CPF system first and review the parameters.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Our starting point is look at the CPF system first, review the parameters.

sections.label: Older workers CPF savings runway
sections.summary: States older workers will not have the runway to accumulate savings through the CPF system.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Older workers will not have the runway to accumulate savings through the CPF system.

sections.label: Self-employed and gig worker CPF
sections.summary: Notes a third group, self-employed persons outside the CPF system, and one move for gig workers to contribute to CPF.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: And then, of course, we have a third group which are self-employed persons who are not part of the CPF system.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: We have made one move for gig workers in working in platform companies to contribute to their CPF.

sections.label: Support for ITE graduates
sections.summary: A support system should help ITE graduates upgrade, reskill and pursue work-study, technical, polytechnic diplomas or degrees.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: But we want to make sure that we are able to help them upgrade, reskill and continue in their careers, whatever they are.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: So, that must mean a very good system of support for an ITE graduate, maybe comes out ITE with a higher NITEC but, eventually, can get a work-study diploma, a technical diploma or even a polytechnic diploma, or maybe even a degree and there must be that system to encourage and support them in their continuous pursuit of new skills.

sections.label: Revenue from proposed system
sections.summary: Ms Hazel Poa's suggestion was addressed from a broader perspective, and more near-term revenue depends on assumptions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: On Ms Hazel Poa's suggestion, when I talked about it not yielding more revenue than our current system, I was referring to it from a broader perspective and not just from a year-to-year perspective.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: So, it can generate more revenue in the near term, perhaps, but it really depends on the assumptions.

sections.label: Purpose of pursuing growth
sections.summary: Growth is pursued as a means to uplift lives and advance the well-being of Singaporeans, not for its own sake.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: As I mentioned in my remarks, we are not pursuing growth for its own sake.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: We want to pursue growth as a means to an end and that end must be to uplift the lives of Singaporeans to advance the well-being of Singaporeans.

sections.label: Temasek inclusion in 2015
sections.summary: Tharman Shanmugaratnam's speech said Temasek's inclusion was deferred when the NIR framework was introduced and would be reviewed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: The Finance Minister said he respectfully disagrees with my characterisation of the move made in 2015 to include Temasek and that this actually was a plan that the Government already had in the works for some time.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: So, I took the opportunity to pull out then Finance Minister Tharman Shanmugaratnam's Second Reading speech on the Constitution of the Republic of Singapore (Amendment) Bill, which effected this change.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: This is what was said: "We had deferred Temasek's inclusion when the NIR framework was first introduced and indicated that we would review this some years after implementation".

sections.label: Staging Temasek incorporation
sections.summary: Staging was wanted because incorporating Temasek into the framework is complex, as Temasek differs from GIC.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: The only reason why we wanted to stage it was because of the complexity of having to incorporate Temasek into the framework because Temasek is quite different from GIC.

sections.label: Sticking to NIR rules
sections.summary: With growing needs, the additional resource helps, but the finalised framework with Temasek should keep to the rules.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: And in recognising that, yes, we have growing needs, this additional resource will be helpful.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: But the point remains, having finalised the framework, with Temasek in as we had originally intended, let us stick to the rules and let us keep that system going for now.
